title: Leadjourney Integration | Attio
description: Ad attribution for your Attio CRM
tagline: Ad attribution for your Attio CRM

segments.t: LeadJourney is an ad-attribution platform that ties every conversion back to the marketing channel, campaign, and ad that drove it.

Connect Attio to LeadJourney and your CRM record events, new people, new deals, deal stage changes, won opportunities, start flowing into LeadJourney as conversions. Every Attio record is automatically matched back to the original click_id, ad, and campaign that generated it, so you can finally answer questions like "which Google Ads campaign produced the deals that closed last month?" or "what's the true CAC by channel including downstream Attio pipeline?"
Built for B2B teams running paid acquisition on Meta, Google, TikTok, LinkedIn, or any other ad platform, and using Attio as their source of truth for revenue.

After you connect your Attio workspace through OAuth, LeadJourney registers a per-workspace webhook subscription on the events you care about (Record Created, Record Updated) for the objects you choose (People, Deals, Companies).
When a matching record event fires in Attio, LeadJourney:
Verifies the webhook signature using the per-subscription secret.
Fetches the full record from Attio's API (and the associated person on Deal events).
Runs your trigger's field-mapping rules to extract identity (email, phone, click_id) and revenue.
Applies any filters you've configured (e.g. only fire when stage = Won).
Dispatches a conversion event into the same attribution pipeline used by every other channel, which matches it against tracked clicks and updates ad-platform performance dashboards.
Everything runs in seconds. Deduplication is handled per-event so Attio's retry semantics never produce double-counted conversions.
From the Apps tab in LeadJourney, click "Connect Attio" and approve the OAuth grant for your workspace.
Click "Add trigger" and pick the Attio event you care about, for example "Deal Updated" if you want to fire a conversion when a deal closes.
Set the Conversion Type (e.g. "Sale", "Booked Demo", "Lead") that this trigger should report as.
Map LeadJourney fields to Attio attribute paths: email → values.email_addresses[0].email_address
revenue → values.value[0].currency_value
click_id → values.click_id[0].value (only present if you've added a custom attribute to capture it)
For Deal triggers, use the `person.` prefix to pull from the associated person (e.g. person.values.email_addresses[0].email_address).
Optionally add filters to gate the trigger, for example, fire only when values.stage[0].status.title equals "Won".
Save. The webhook subscription is updated automatically and events start flowing immediately.
You can pause, edit, or delete any trigger at any time. Disconnecting Attio cleans up the webhook on Attio's side automatically.

title: GeoMaps Integration | Attio
description: Turn your Attio CRM into an interactive map
tagline: Turn your Attio CRM into an interactive map

segments.t: GeoMaps turns your Attio workspace into an interactive map, with no GIS skills required. It places your people, companies, deals and custom objects on a live map that stays in sync with Attio. From there you can filter and colour-code records by any attribute, find what's nearby, plan optimized multi-stop routes, draw territories and drive-time areas, build heatmaps and publish shareable, embeddable maps.

It works both ways: edit a record on the map or in the table and the change is saved in Attio. Reps in the field use the GeoMaps mobile app (iOS and Android) to navigate to customers, update records and check in after a visit, with the visit note saved on the Attio record. It's built for sales, field and operations teams who want to see and act on their Attio data geographically.
You connect GeoMaps to your Attio workspace with a secure sign-in (no token to copy). GeoMaps reads:
• People, Companies and Deals: names, address and location attributes, and the attributes you choose to filter or colour by
• Your custom objects: any object with address or location data
• Workspace members: so owner and user fields show names
GeoMaps geocodes the addresses into map coordinates and keeps the map up to date as your Attio data changes.
What GeoMaps writes to Attio, only when someone does it in GeoMaps:
• Record edits: a change made in GeoMaps (map popup, table, bulk actions or the mobile app) is saved to that record in Attio. Location, linked-record and user attributes stay read-only.
• New records: a record added in GeoMaps is created in Attio.

• Check-in notes: when a rep checks in on a record in the mobile app, GeoMaps creates one note on that record with the visit note, the rep's name and the time. GeoMaps only creates notes. It never reads, edits or deletes your existing notes.
GeoMaps never deletes Attio records, and you can disconnect at any time.
To use this app you need a GeoMaps account. It starts with a 14-day free trial, no credit card required. Setup takes a couple of minutes:
Create or log in to your GeoMaps account at app.geomaps.co.
Open Data Sources, choose Attio and click Connect Attio.
Sign in to your Attio workspace and approve the access GeoMaps asks for.
Choose the Attio objects you want to map (e.g. People, Companies, Deals) and confirm the address field. GeoMaps imports and geocodes them onto an interactive map.
Already connected before November 2026? Reconnect once (Data Sources → your Attio source → Settings → Reconnect) to allow check-in notes. Until then, check-ins are kept in GeoMaps only.
No coding or GIS experience is required.

description: Stop guessing how messy your Attio is

segments.t: Audit for Attio is a free, read-only diagnostic for your Attio workspace. Connect once and four minutes later you get a private, shareable report with a health score, a schema diagram, an attribute density map, and 50+ ranked findings that name every duplicate, every stale deal, every dead field, and every ownership gap in your CRM. Each finding is severity ranked, comes with the affected record count, and links to the exact records driving it. Where we can attach a dollar figure or hours-saved estimate, we do.

The audit was built by Dialed Technologies for revenue operations leads, founders, and CRM admins on mid-market teams who use Attio. It is the fastest way to find out where your workspace is leaking trust before the next QBR, board review, or pipeline cleanup sprint. Reports include a ready-to-paste Slack summary, a PDF export, and an LLM-ready markdown export so the findings travel.
Common use cases:
Pre-QBR sanity check on data quality and pipeline health
Onboarding into a workspace someone else built
Quarterly hygiene review before a big migration or integration
Diligence on a workspace inherited through an acquisition
Building the case for a CRM cleanup project with your team

The audit itself is free, with no upsell required to read every finding. If you want help fixing what we surface, Dialed runs paid engagements separately (dedup, enrichment, ownership remediation, pipeline modelling, integration repair).

Audit for Attio uses Attio's OAuth flow with read-only scopes to fetch your workspace configuration and a representative sample of records. The token literally cannot write to your workspace, because no write scopes are on it.
What we read from your workspace:
Objects, attributes, and select options (
object_configuration:read
Records on every object (
record_permission:read
Lists and their attribute schemas (
list_configuration:read
Entries on every list (
list_entry:read
Workspace members and their access levels (
user_management:read
Webhook endpoints and recent delivery state (
webhook:read
Notes attached to records (
note:read
Tasks and assignments (
task:read
Meetings synced into the workspace (
meeting:read
Call recording metadata, not audio (
call_recording:read
Comment threads (
comment:read
File metadata, not file contents (
file:read
What we never request: any
:write
scope, your Attio password (OAuth never sees it), or billing data.
After OAuth, the audit pipeline runs in four phases:
Fetch workspace configuration and a representative record sample
Fetch activity data (notes, tasks, meetings, comments, recordings)
Run 50+ analyzer functions over the fetched snapshot
Generate the report, send the email, and stamp the share link
The whole pipeline finishes in about four minutes for a workspace under 10,000 records and scales linearly from there. Larger workspaces see a warning on the loading screen with the expected wait.
Storage and retention:
OAuth tokens encrypted with AES-256-GCM in a US-region Postgres
Raw API snapshots retained up to 30 days so the analyzers can re-run without re-hitting the Attio API, then purged
Unsaved reports deleted seven days after the audit finishes
Saved reports kept until you delete them from My reports
Anonymized aggregate benchmarks only if you opt in (default no)

Reports are private by default. The share URL is gated by either a session cookie or a magic link scoped to a specific email. Visitors without either are routed to a request-access page that pings the workspace owner for an invite.
No configuration is required to run the audit. The product is free, no paid plan is necessary, and there is no setup inside Attio beyond the one-time OAuth consent.
To run an audit:
Visit
dialed.tech/audit
Click "Start free audit"
You will be redirected to Attio's standard OAuth consent screen, which lists the exact read-only scopes we request
Approve the connection
(Optional) Answer two questions on the loading screen so the report personalizes itself to your primary use case
Wait about four minutes while the audit runs
Read the report at its shareable URL, or wait for the email
To invite teammates:
Open the report
Click the Actions menu in the top right
Choose "Manage access"
Enter teammate emails and choose viewer or admin access
Each invitee gets a magic link scoped to that workspace
To revoke access:
The owner can revoke any invite from the Manage access dialog
Disconnecting the Attio app from Attio's settings revokes our OAuth token; we stop calling the API and remove the token on next use
Email
contact@dialed.tech
to fully delete the audit, findings, and tokens within seven days
There is no Attio-side configuration object to create, no custom attributes to add, and no webhook to wire up. The audit is self-contained.

title: Falora Integration | Attio
description: Control Your Growth
tagline: Control Your Growth

segments.t: Falora connects ad experiment performance to CRM pipeline data. The Attio integration lets Falora read your deal pipeline and match contacts to ad experiments via UTM tags - so you can see which experiments actually generate leads, MQLs, SQLs, and revenue.

Falora never stores contact information. During each sync, Falora reads contacts and deals from Attio, counts how many reached each pipeline stage per experiment, and writes only the aggregated numbers back to its own database. No names, emails, or personal data leave your Attio workspace.
Once connected, Falora runs a daily sync against your Attio workspace. The process works in four steps:
Fetch contacts with UTM data.
Falora queries Attio for all people where your configured UTM field is populated. Only the UTM value, pipeline stage, and deal value are read - no other contact data is pulled.
Resolve pipeline stages.

Each contact's associated Deal is checked to determine their current stage. Falora translates this into your mapped canonical stage (Lead, MQL, SQL, Opportunity, Deal Won, or Deal Lost) using the mapping you configured during setup.
Aggregate per experiment.
Contacts are grouped by their UTM value and counted per stage. Counting is cumulative - an SQL is also counted as an MQL and a Lead. Deal values are summed for won deals.
Write metrics, discard contacts.
Only the aggregated counts and revenue per experiment are stored in Falora. The individual contact data is discarded after processing. Nothing is written back to Attio.

A manual "Sync Now" button is available for on-demand refreshes. When you drill down into an experiment's contacts in Falora, that data is fetched live from Attio and displayed in-session - it's never cached or persisted on Falora's side.

An Attio account with permission to install integrations

Map your pipeline stages.
Choose your deal pipeline, then assign each stage to a Falora funnel stage (Lead, MQL, SQL, Opportunity, Deal Won, Deal Lost, or Skip). At least two stages must be mapped.
Test the connection.
Falora runs a sample sync and shows a preview of matched experiments with their stage counts, so you can verify the mapping is correct before activating.

Daily sync starts immediately. You can adjust field and stage mappings at any time without disconnecting.

title: Whalesync Integration | Attio
description: Two-way sync with Airtable, Notion, Sheets, and more
tagline: Two-way sync with Airtable, Notion, Sheets, and more

segments.t: Whalesync keeps Attio in sync with the tools your team already runs on. Connect Attio to Postgres, Supabase, Airtable, Notion, Google Sheets, and more, and Whalesync keeps both sides current. There is nothing to script, no export to schedule, and no engineering time to book.

Sync runs in both directions. A person created in Attio lands in your warehouse within a minute. A plan change written by your product database updates the matching company in Attio. You set the direction for each pair of tables, so you can push one way, pull the other, or keep both sides equal.
Whalesync matches records that already exist instead of creating duplicates, so you can switch it on over data you have been collecting for years rather than starting from an empty workspace.

It covers the whole workspace: people, companies and deals, every custom object you have built, your lists, and the notes and tasks attached to your records. Custom attributes are picked up on their own as soon as you create them, and record references sync as real links rather than as text, so the relationships between objects survive the trip. Workspace members are read as well, so record owners resolve to real people on both sides.

Teams use Whalesync to load product usage into Attio so sales can see which accounts are active, to push closed deals into a warehouse for revenue reporting, to create follow-up tasks and log notes on the right record from their own systems, and to keep Attio aligned with the spreadsheets and databases that operations still depend on. It is just as often used in the other direction, by teams who have years of history in a database and want Attio to be the place their colleagues actually work.

Whalesync syncs in both directions by default, or in one direction if you prefer. Edits made in Attio and edits made in the connected tool both propagate, usually within a minute. Direction is set per pair of tables, so one object can be read-only while another is fully two-way.

Sync people, companies, and deals, along with every custom object and list in your workspace, and the notes and tasks attached to them. Whalesync reads your schema directly from Attio rather than working from a fixed list, so an object you create this afternoon is available to map straight away, as are any attributes you add to it.

Record references sync as real links rather than as text. A deal stays attached to its company and a person stays attached to their employer, on both sides of the sync, so the copy in your database is queryable rather than a flat export.

Notes and tasks sync as tables of their own, attached to the record they belong to. A task created in your project tool or database appears in Attio on the right person or company, with its due date and assignee, and marking it done on either side marks it done on the other. Notes work the same way: a call summary written by your support tool lands on the account in Attio, and a note edited in Attio updates the copy in your database. Because these are two-way, Whalesync creates, updates, and removes notes and tasks in Attio when the connected tool does, which is why it asks for write access to both.

Choose exactly which attributes sync and how they pair with columns in the other tool. Whalesync proposes matches by name and you can change or remove any of them. Anything you leave unmapped is never read and never written, which makes it safe to sync one part of a record and leave the rest alone.

Point a sync at an empty database and Whalesync creates a table for every object you picked, with a column for each attribute and the right type on each column. There is no schema to write up front and no migration to maintain as your Attio workspace changes.

Sync a subset of records with filters instead of the whole object. Pause any sync from the dashboard without losing its configuration. Deletes can be held for review before they are applied, so a bad import on one side cannot quietly empty a table on the other.

Whalesync registers Attio webhooks, so changes are picked up as they happen rather than waiting for the next scheduled poll. If a webhook is ever missed, a background pass reconciles both sides, so the two do not drift.
Setting up a sync takes a few minutes and no code.
Create a Whalesync account at whalesync.com and start a new sync.
Choose Attio as one side of the sync. Whalesync sends you to Attio’s authorization screen, where you approve access for the workspace you want to sync.
Choose the other side, such as Postgres, Supabase, Airtable, Notion or Google Sheets, and connect it the same way.

Pick the tables to sync. On the Attio side these are your objects and lists: people, companies, deals, any custom object, and any list you have built, plus your notes and tasks. If the other side is an empty database, let Whalesync create the tables for you.
Map attributes to columns. Whalesync proposes matches by name, and you can change any of them or leave attributes out entirely. Unmapped attributes are never read or written.
Choose a direction for each pair of tables: two-way, or one-way into or out of Attio.
Turn the sync on.

blocks.text: What happens on the first run

segments.t: Whalesync loads the records that already exist before it starts watching for changes. It matches rather than duplicates wherever it can, so running it against a workspace that is already full of data does not produce a second copy of everything. Large objects take a while on this first pass; after that, changes arrive as they happen.

Mappings can be edited at any time, and new attributes can be added to a running sync without rebuilding it. Pausing keeps the configuration and stops the traffic. Disconnecting the workspace ends the sync and leaves every record in Attio exactly as it is; nothing is removed on either side.

Users are provisioned as non-admin members by default. To provision someone as an admin, set their role to
admin
in your IDP before assigning them.
How a user is added depends on their email domain:
Verified domain:
The user is added to the workspace directly and receives an email notifying them they've been added. New Attio users also receive a welcome email.
Non-verified domain:
The user receives a workspace invite and is added once they accept it.
Removing or deactivating a user in your IDP suspends their Attio workspace membership immediately and revokes their session.
It’s not possible to delete or downgrade the last remaining admin in a workspace. First, give another member admin access.
Set and update roles using the
roles
attribute in your IDP. Attio supports two roles:
member
and
admin
. An unrecognized role value defaults to member. If both roles are assigned to the same user, admin takes precedence.
SCIM groups map to Attio teams. Pushing a group from your IDP to Attio creates a new team, or you can link an IDP group to an existing team.

blocks.text: How Attio and your IDP work together

segments.t: Your IDP is the source of truth for any members and teams provisioned through it. If a change is made directly in Attio, such as updating a role or team membership, your IDP will reconcile it back to its own state on the next sync.
Any members or teams not currently managed by your IDP can still be managed freely from within Attio and won't be affected by syncs.
You will need to be on the Entreprise plan and be a workspace admin to set up SCIM.

Click on "Authenticate with Attio". This will open up a page for you to login with Attio. After login, you will see a request to give the app access to a workspace.

title: OneCLI Integration | Attio
description: AI agent gateway for secure, scoped API access to Attio
tagline: AI agent gateway for secure, scoped API access to Attio

segments.t: When your team uses AI agents (Claude, GPT, Cursor, Copilot, or custom agents), those agents often need to read contacts, update deals, create notes, or manage tasks in your CRM. OneCLI sits between the agent and Attio's API, injecting credentials on-the-fly and enforcing fine-grained permissions per agent.
With OneCLI + Attio, you can:
Let AI agents query contacts, companies, and deals without giving them your API key
Scope each agent to specific operations (e.g., read-only CRM access for a research agent, read-write for a sales automation agent)
Connect multiple Attio workspaces and route requests to the right one
Monitor every API call agents make to your Attio workspace in real time
Revoke access instantly without rotating credentials
OneCLI handles OAuth token management, automatic token refresh, and credential encryption. Your team connects once and agents get seamless access.
Connect your Attio workspace - From the OneCLI dashboard, click "Connect" on the Attio integration. You'll be redirected to Attio to authorize access. OneCLI requests only the scopes you've approved.

Assign permissions per agent - Each AI agent in OneCLI gets its own API key. You control which Attio operations each agent can perform. For example, allow one agent to read contacts but block it from deleting records.
Agents call Attio through OneCLI - Instead of calling
api.attio.com
directly, agents route requests through the OneCLI gateway. The gateway injects your Attio credentials into each request, enforces permission rules, and logs the call.
Automatic token refresh - Attio OAuth tokens expire after about 1 hour. OneCLI's gateway automatically refreshes tokens before they expire, so agents
never encounter auth errors.
Monitor and audit - Every API call is logged with the agent identity, endpoint, method, and timestamp. Review activity in the OneCLI dashboard or export logs.

Navigate to the Integrations page in your OneCLI dashboard. Find Attio and click "Connect." You'll be redirected to Attio to authorize OneCLI. Sign in to the Attio workspace you want to connect and approve the requested permissions.
Step 2: Configure agent permissions

After connecting, go to the Attio integration detail page. You'll see toggleable permission groups (Records, Lists, Notes, Tasks, etc.). Enable the permissions each agent needs. By default, all permissions are granted. Narrow them down per agent for least-privilege access.
Step 3: Use with your agents

Give your AI agent the OneCLI API key (starts with oc_). Configure the agent to route Attio API calls through the OneCLI gateway. The agent makes standard Attio API calls and OneCLI handles authentication transparently.
Bring Your Own Credentials (optional)
If you prefer to use your own Attio OAuth app instead of OneCLI's shared app, go to the Attio integration settings and enter your Client ID and Client
Secret. OneCLI will use your credentials for the OAuth flow and token refresh.
Disconnecting
To revoke OneCLI's access, click "Disconnect" on the Attio integration page. You can also revoke access from Attio's side in your workspace settings under Connected Apps.

segments.t: Cal.com Sync is an app that automatically syncs Cal.com bookings into Attio.

This gives sales, support, and customer success teams better visibility into scheduled interactions with contacts, prospects, and customers.
Cal.com Sync runs in the background and handles key booking updates automatically, including new bookings, reschedules, cancellations, and no-show changes.
You can customize field mappings and filtering options so the sync matches your team’s workflow and data requirements.
Cal.com Sync can be used to track sales calls, customer onboarding sessions, support consultations, and other scheduled meetings without manual data entry.
Cal.com Sync keeps your Attio CRM updated when bookings change in Cal.com.
Cal.com Sync monitors these booking events in Cal.com.
Booking created. Creates a new entry in Attio when a meeting is scheduled.
Booking rescheduled. Updates the existing entry, or creates a new one based on your configuration.
Booking cancelled. Marks the entry as cancelled and captures the cancellation reason when available.
No-show updated. Tracks when an attendee does not show up to a scheduled meeting.
For each booking, Cal.com Sync can capture the following information.
Event details such as title, description, unique identifier, start time, end time, timezone, location, and meeting link.
Attendee details such as name, email address, and timezone.
Organizer details such as name and email address.
Booking status such as active, pending, cancelled, rescheduled, or no-show.
Additional context such as event type ID, booking form responses, cancellation reasons, and reschedule information.
Metadata such as the last updated timestamp.
Cal.com Sync can automatically create person records in Attio for meeting attendees who do not already exist in your CRM. This helps keep booking records connected to the right contacts.
You can disable automatic person creation if you only want to sync bookings for people who already exist in Attio.
Cal.com Sync can create a dedicated Cal.com Bookings list in Attio with the required attributes. You can also configure the app to use an existing list.
Each booking entry is linked to the related person record, making it easier to view a contact’s full meeting history.
Cal.com Sync uses Cal.com webhooks to receive updates when bookings change. This keeps Attio up to date without manual refreshes or scheduled polling.

segments.t: Quotient is an AI-native platform and intelligent agent in one; built to plan and execute campaigns across email, social, blog, and events, without the fragmented tools you've outgrown.

At its core, Quotient is an AI demand marketing platform. It brings everything that attracts customers: blogs, social posts, email, webinars and events, and brand-building, into one integrated workspace powered by your AI model of choice (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini).

You work with Quotient like a coworker. Describe what you want in plain English, and it takes it from there. The interface pairs a traditional app panel for managing campaigns, blogs, and emails with a conversational chat panel alongside it. Anything you can do in the app directly, you can also do by asking the Quotient agent.

Campaigns organize your marketing around a central goal, like a feature launch or event. Each is a coordinated set of tasks and deliverables moving through a clear workflow. Deliverables are the real assets Quotient creates and ships: blog posts, email broadcasts, marketing events, automated flows, and social posts for X, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok. Ask Quotient to build a campaign end to end: it writes the brief, breaks the work into tasks, sets the timeline, and produces each deliverable.

Quotient gets smarter over time, drawing on a Knowledge Store of brand information, recording memories of your preferences, and using tools to search the web and pull from your audience of people and companies.

And you're not limited to Quotient's own interface: with our MCP integration, you can use Quotient directly inside Claude Cowork. Planning campaigns, writing content, and managing your audience is now achievable without leaving your Claude interface.
The result is a single platform where strategy, content, and execution live together, replacing the patchwork of disconnected marketing tools with one AI that plans, writes, and ships.

Reps stop writing follow-ups.
The recap, the plan and the best-fit case studies are drafted from the call, and each new call suggests updates. Reps review instead of writing.
Your champion sells it for you.
They forward the room or invite colleagues from it, so the people who weren’t on the call hear the same story. Each buyer who signs in is added to Attio automatically.
Next steps get done.
The action plan is shared with the buyer and synced with Attio tasks. A step finished on either side is finished on both.
Buyer activity you can sort and automate on.
Engagement score, last buyer view, active stakeholders and plan completion land on the deal as Attio fields. Sort your pipeline by them, or use them to trigger your own Attio workflows.
foyai never sends anything to a buyer on its own. Every room waits for your rep.
Get Pro free for 30 days, no card, or use Free forever. The rooms you publish stay live either way. Want a hand? Book a 30-minute setup with our team when you first sign in.
See a real room the way your buyer would: foyai.com/see-a-room.
Foyai runs on the calls and records you already keep in Attio. Connect once, and here's the flow from deal to published room.
1. Pick a deal.
Choose a company or deal and select the call(s) you want to build from. Foyai matches the recording to the right account using your linked records and meeting participants.

A recap of what the buyer told you, written from the call

the moment a buyer opens a room

segments.t: The Partnero and Attio integration automatically keeps your partner program and CRM in sync. Partners, customers, and transactions are shared between both platforms in real time, so your data stays consistent without manual updates.

The integration works in both directions. Records created or updated in Partnero are pushed to Attio. Actions taken in Attio, like closing a deal, create transactions and trigger partner commissions in Partnero. Each program connects to Attio separately using OAuth 2.0.

When a partner, customer, or transaction is created or updated in Partnero, the record is automatically sent to Attio. Partners can be mapped to any Attio object: People, Companies, or a custom object. Customer sync is optional: if your customers already exist in Attio, you can skip this to avoid duplicates. Transactions create corresponding Deals in Attio, including amount, currency, and a link to the customer record.

When a deal reaches your configured "won" stage in Attio, Partnero automatically creates a transaction and triggers the partner's commission. Customer records created or updated in Attio are also synced back to Partnero, matched by email.
A field mapping interface lets you control which fields are synced for partners, customers, and deals. Partner and customer mapping are both optional; configure only what you need.

The integration includes safeguards to prevent duplicate records and sync loops. Each transaction is tied to a unique Attio deal ID, and outbound records are tagged to distinguish them from records originating in Attio.

title: Probo Access Review Integration | Attio
description: Bring Attio workspace members into your access reviews
tagline: Bring Attio workspace members into your access reviews

segments.t: Probo is the open-source compliance platform that helps teams achieve SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, and CCPA certifications without the usual chaos. Connect Probo to your identity providers, code platforms, and SaaS tools to automate access reviews, evidence collection, and continuous control monitoring. Probo combines the platform, expert auditors, and concierge guidance to take you from kickoff to audit-ready in weeks, not months. Backed by Y Combinator and trusted by 100+ companies in 20+ countries.

This app connects Attio to Probo as an access review source. Probo reads your Attio workspace members, their access level, and when they joined, so every member of your CRM appears in your scheduled access reviews alongside the rest of your stack. Reviewers see who holds admin rights, who has been suspended, and record an approve or revoke decision against each seat as audit evidence.
Probo requests read-only access to user management and nothing else. It never reads your records, lists, notes, emails, or any customer data held in Attio.

Probo Access Review reads a single endpoint, GET /v2/workspace_members, using the user_management:read scope. For each workspace member it collects the first and last name, the email address, the access level, the workspace member ID, and the date the member was created. It writes nothing back to Attio.

Attio does not delete workspace members, so a member who loses access keeps their record with the access level set to suspended. Probo reports those seats as inactive rather than dropping them, which is what an auditor needs to see. Attio exposes no last sign-in and no multi-factor status, so Probo leaves those fields blank rather than guessing at them.

You need a Probo organization and an Attio workspace administrator to authorize the connection. In Probo, go to Access Review, then Connections, find Attio and choose OAuth. Attio asks you to approve read access to user management, and the source then appears in your campaigns as Attio followed by your workspace name. A workspace access token created under Settings, Developers, Access tokens with User Management set to Read works as an alternative to OAuth.

title: Round Robin Pro Integration | Attio
description: Automatically assign users to records and list items
tagline: Automatically assign users to records and list items

segments.t: Round Robin Pro helps Attio teams assign records and list entries to workspace members using reusable round-robin and weighted templates.
Instead of manually choosing an owner for each new lead, account, user, task, or list entry, workspace admins can create assignment templates in Attio settings and use them inside Attio workflows.
Each workflow run selects the next eligible teammate, updates the configured Attio User field, and makes the selected assignee available to later workflow steps.
Templates can use round-robin distribution for equal assignment, or weighted distribution when some teammates should receive a larger share.
You can also add optional availability settings for individual workspace members, including active status, timezone, working days, and working hours.
Round Robin Pro keeps an audit log so workspace admins can see who made changes to templates or availability settings.
Round Robin Pro is designed for teams that want consistent ownership rules across sales, support, operations, onboarding, and internal workflows.
It works with standard Attio object records and list entries, so your team can assign the records it already uses without moving the process outside Attio.
A workspace admin creates one or more templates from the Round Robin Pro settings page.
Each template defines the workspace members who can receive assignments, the distribution model, and any optional availability rules.
Round Robin Pro adds a custom workflow block to Attio called "Assign round robin user". Using the block, you can select a template to run when the block is triggered.
When an Attio workflow reaches the Round Robin Pro block, the app loads the selected template and checks which members are currently eligible.
If at least one member is available, Round Robin Pro selects the next assignee, updates the configured Attio User field, and returns the Assignee selected outcome.
The selected assignee is available to later workflow blocks.
You can use the selected assignee in steps such as sending a Slack notification, creating a task, branching by outcome, or updating additional fields.
If no member is available, the workflow follows the No assignee available outcome.
This lets you create a separate workflow path for cases where no eligible assignee is found because of availability settings, inactive participants, or template configuration.
Round Robin Pro supports assignments for object records and list entries.
Object records. Assign a User field directly on an Attio object record, such as a Company, Person, Deal, User, or custom object record.

List entries. Assign a User field on an Attio list entry. The workflow can use a list-entry trigger or a record variable from the trigger, and the app updates the selected User field on the matching entry.
You can watch a demo of how the app works here:
https://tinyurl.com/round-robin-demo
To configure Round Robin Pro, install the app in Attio, create an assignment template, and add the workflow block to the relevant Attio workflow.
Install Round Robin Pro in your Attio workspace.
Open Workspace Settings > Apps > Round Robin Pro.
Create a round-robin or weighted assignment template from the Round Robin Pro settings page.
Select the Attio workspace members who should receive assignments.
Choose the distribution model, either round robin or weighted.
For weighted templates, make sure all weighted values add up to 100%.
Optionally add availability settings for members who should only receive assignments during specific working days and hours.
After creating a template, add Round Robin Pro to an Attio workflow.
Create or edit an Attio workflow.
Add the Assign round robin user block after a record or list-entry trigger.
Select the assignment template.
Select the target record or list entry. Use variables
For Lists, select
Use a variable > Record added to list > Created Entry
For Records (eg. Users), select
Use a variable > Record created > Created User
Select the Attio User field that should receive the assignee.
Publish the workflow.
Round Robin Pro includes a 14-day free trial. Paid plans are managed from the app’s settings page in Attio.

Object configuration, read: to list deal stages and People attributes
User management, read: to let you pick the deal owner
Notes, read and write: to save the form answers as a note

Save and publish the automation, then use Test lead to send a sample lead to Attio.

To stop sending leads, pause or delete the automation in Targenix. To revoke access, delete the Attio connection on the Connections page in Targenix, or remove the app from your Attio workspace settings.

segments.t: Qobra is a sales compensation platform that automates commission calculations and gives revenue teams real-time visibility on their earnings. Finance and RevOps teams design commission plans without code; sales reps track their commissions live instead of waiting for end-of-quarter spreadsheets.

With the Attio integration, your Attio workspace becomes the source of truth for compensation. Qobra imports your objects and lists, deals, companies, pipeline stages, custom attributes, and matches records to their owners, so commissions are always calculated on up-to-date CRM data and attributed to the right rep. No CSV exports, no manual reconciliation.
Once your Attio workspace is connected, Qobra works in four steps:
1. Automatic discovery of your data model.

Qobra reads your Attio objects (standard and custom, Companies, People, Deals, or anything you've built) and your Lists, along with all their attributes: custom attributes, select and status options, currencies, record references, and enriched attributes. Your Attio structure appears in Qobra exactly as you designed it, nothing to remodel.
2. Lists as first-class data.

Many Attio teams run their pipeline through Lists rather than objects. Qobra imports each List as its own data table, including its stage/status attributes and the link to the parent record, so the pipeline data that drives your commissions is fully available in your plans.
3. Continuous sync.

Records are imported and refreshed automatically, so commission calculations always run on current data. Enriched and system attributes are synced too, flagged as read-only. The integration is strictly read-only: Qobra never writes anything to your Attio workspace.
4. Automatic owner resolution.
Your Attio workspace members are matched to Qobra users, so every imported record resolves to its owner. When a deal closes in Attio, the commission lands on the right rep in Qobra, automatically.

From there, you build compensation plans on live Attio data: targets, rates, accelerators, team splits. Reps follow their earnings in real time, managers pilot performance, and finance validates and exports payouts with full audit trail.

In Qobra, go to
Settings → Integrations
and select
Attio
. You'll be redirected to Attio to authorize the connection.

Review the read-only permissions Qobra requests, access to your objects, lists, records, and workspace members, and approve. Qobra only ever reads from your workspace; it never creates, edits, or deletes anything in Attio. Attio redirects you back to Qobra automatically.
3. Choose what to import.
Select the objects and lists you want to sync (Companies, People, Deals, your pipeline lists, custom objects…) and pick the attributes relevant to your compensation plans.
4. Map your team.
Your Attio workspace members are matched to your Qobra users, automatically by email, adjustable manually, so every record resolves to the right owner.
5. Launch the first sync.
Your Attio data flows into Qobra and is ready to power your commission plans. From there, records refresh automatically to keep calculations up to date.

segments.t: Regional Task Queue turns up to the first 1,999 incomplete Attio tasks assigned to the current member into a focused queue for regional execution. Everything stays inside Attio. Open the queue from companies or people, review one slice at a time and mark each task complete as you work. No external account, workspace setting or service connection is required.

Regional Task Queue loads up to the first 1,999 incomplete tasks assigned to the current Attio member. The final result of the fourth API page is used only to detect whether more tasks exist. When the result is truncated, the dialog states exactly how many were loaded. The app derives a region from the primary location of a linked person or company. When a person has no location, the app can use the location of their linked company. A leading square bracket label in the task title becomes its type. Tasks without that label appear as UNCATEGORIZED. Within each type, dated tasks appear in deadline order and tasks without a deadline appear last.
Open companies or people.
Click Show menu.
Choose Regional task queue.
Choose a region.
Choose a type.
Select a task.
Click Mark complete.
Repeat to process the displayed queue.

Before completion, the app verifies that the selected task is still incomplete and assigned to the active member. It marks only that task complete, refreshes the queue and keeps the member in the same focused workflow.

No external account, API key, service connection or workspace setting is required. After an Attio admin installs the app and approves its permissions, members can open companies or people and launch Regional task queue from Show menu.

User Management read access identifies the active workspace member. Records read access retrieves the names and primary locations of linked people and companies. Object Configuration read access resolves linked object identifiers. Tasks read and write access lists the active member’s incomplete tasks, verifies the selected task and marks that task complete. The app does not create, delete or edit people or company records.

For clear type groups, begin a task title with a square bracket label such as [CALL], [EMAIL] or [FOLLOW-UP]. Any task without a leading label remains available under UNCATEGORIZED. Region groups use the primary location on linked people or companies. The app performs no scheduled processing and makes no background writes.

title: CoreSpeed Integration | Attio
description: Connect Attio to secure AI agents and workflows
tagline: Connect Attio to secure AI agents and workflows

segments.t: CoreSpeed connects AI agents and automated workflows to your Attio workspace through an OAuth connector. Agents use the MCP interface hosted by CoreSpeed; CoreSpeed then calls Attio's REST API with the workspace permissions you authorize. This app does not register an MCP server with Attio or add an MCP endpoint to Ask Attio. Use the connector to discover CRM objects and lists, look up workspace members, find records, and create or update records in existing objects.
Connect an Attio workspace in CoreSpeed, then use its seven Attio tools from a CoreSpeed-connected agent.

Read CRM context: list_objects discovers available objects, including people, companies, and custom objects; list_lists reads list definitions; query_records and get_record retrieve records from the object you specify. Listing lists does not read or modify list entries.

Look up teammates: list_workspace_members reads the workspace member directory, including member names, email addresses, and IDs. An agent can answer who belongs to the workspace or resolve a member ID to a person. This feature requires user_management:read; it does not invite members or change their access.

Write CRM records: create_record creates a record in an existing object, and update_record changes the supplied attributes on an existing record. Object configuration and list configuration are read-only.

Data flows from the agent through CoreSpeed to Attio. Attio returns the requested data through CoreSpeed to the agent. Writes send the requested record values in the opposite direction. These are tool-triggered requests, not an automatic background sync.
Sign in to CoreSpeed and open Connectors > Attio at https://app.corespeed.io/connectors/attio.
Choose Connect (or Add under Accounts if you already have a connection), then choose the account visibility offered by CoreSpeed.

Sign in to Attio, select the workspace, and review the requested access: records read-write, object configuration read, list configuration read, and user management read. Approve the OAuth request to return to CoreSpeed.
Confirm the connected workspace/account and note its alias in CoreSpeed. For a private connection, use the same CoreSpeed user and organization in your agent.

Connect your MCP-compatible agent to CoreSpeed using the CoreSpeed client setup guide. The MCP endpoint is hosted by CoreSpeed, not Attio. Ask the agent to list Attio objects or look up workspace members, then query records or request a specific create/update action.
Manage, reconnect, or disconnect the Attio account from its CoreSpeed connector page.
See the Attio-specific documentation below for tool behavior, permissions, and data flow.

title: Stripe Invoicing Integration | Attio
description: Automate billing with Stripe invoicing directly in Attio
tagline: Automate billing with Stripe invoicing directly in Attio

segments.t: Stripe Invoicing brings billing into the records where your team already works. From a person record, an operator can create a Stripe invoice using that person's email and name. From a company record, they pick one of the company's associated people and invoice them. Either way the Stripe customer is resolved from the email address: an existing customer with that email is reused, or a new one is created, so you never end up with duplicate customers. Line items come from your existing Stripe products and prices, or from one-off custom products and prices typed inline. The operator sets a due date and either finalizes the invoice or finalizes and emails it through Stripe in the same step.

The app can also sync Stripe invoices back into Attio. When sync is enabled it maintains an invoices object linked to people, registers a Stripe webhook, and mirrors invoices in real time as they are finalized, paid, fail payment, or are voided. Each synced invoice is matched to a person by the Stripe customer email, with an optional setting to create the person automatically when no match exists. A manual backfill pulls every historical invoice in, and a settings panel reports connection, webhook, and schema health, including a banner that lists any Stripe permissions the connected key is missing.

Stripe Invoicing also plugs into Attio workflows. It adds trigger blocks that start a workflow when a Stripe invoice is finalized, paid, fails payment, or is voided, and step blocks that create a Stripe customer, create a Stripe invoice, or update an invoice's status from inside a workflow. Teams can build automations such as notifying an owner the moment an invoice is paid or creating an invoice when a deal reaches a stage.

Stripe Invoicing is workspace-scoped and uses your existing Stripe API key. Teams that only want to send invoices can switch sync off entirely (send-only mode) and the create flow and workflow blocks keep working. Teams that want a billing mirror in Attio can map the sync onto a brand-new invoices object or onto an object they already have. It suits professional services, agencies, and B2B SaaS teams that run customer relationships in Attio and bill through Stripe.
Stripe Invoicing adds a Create Invoice action to both the people object and the companies object, plus a Sync Stripe Invoices action, a set of Stripe workflow blocks, and a workspace settings panel.

On a person record, the dialog reads the person's name and email and uses them directly. On a company record, the dialog lists the company's associated people and asks the operator to choose one; that person's name and email then drive the invoice. The Stripe customer is resolved server-side from the email: the app finds an existing customer with that email or creates one, matching on email rather than name so customers are not duplicated.

The operator then builds line items. Each line item references a Stripe product and price read from the connected account, or a one-off custom product and unit price typed inline (the app creates the Stripe product and price on the fly). A due date sets the payment terms, and the operator either finalizes and emails the invoice or finalizes only and shares the hosted invoice URL manually.

When sync is enabled, connecting the app creates an invoices object linked to people and asks Stripe to notify Attio whenever an invoice changes. (That notification is called a webhook: Stripe sends Attio a short message the moment an invoice is finalized, paid, fails payment, or is voided, so Attio stays up to date without anyone refreshing it.) The app confirms each message genuinely came from Stripe before acting on it, then creates or updates the matching invoice record. Records are keyed on the Stripe invoice id, so the same invoice is never duplicated and a late or out-of-order message cannot overwrite newer data; each record is linked to a person by the customer email. The Sync Stripe Invoices action imports your entire invoice history in the background and picks up where it left off if it is interrupted, so even a large back catalog imports reliably.

For automation, the app adds Stripe workflow blocks. Four trigger blocks start a workflow when a Stripe invoice is finalized, paid, fails payment, or is voided; they all listen through the same Stripe notification described above, so adding a trigger never opens a second connection to Stripe. Three step blocks run inside a workflow to create a Stripe customer (or update the one matched by email), create a Stripe invoice, or update an invoice's status: finalize, send, pay, void, or mark uncollectible.

The schema is configurable. If the target object already exists, the operator maps each synced field to their own names in workspace settings, and the app reuses that object and adds only the attributes that are missing. A master toggle turns sync off for send-only workspaces. When the app connects, it checks the Stripe key for any missing permissions and lists them in the settings panel rather than failing silently. Your Stripe and Attio credentials are never exposed in the dialog, and errors surface as clear messages to the operator.

Stripe Invoicing requires a Stripe API key scoped to the resources the app touches: customers, products, prices, invoice items, invoices, and (for sync) webhook endpoints. Follow these steps to install and configure the app.
Install Stripe Invoicing from the Attio App Store into the workspace where you want to create invoices.

Create a restricted Stripe API key in your Stripe dashboard at Developers, API keys, Create restricted key. Grant write access to Customers, Products, Prices, Invoice items, and Invoices, plus read and write on Webhook endpoints. Read access alone is not sufficient, because the app creates invoices and registers a webhook on your behalf.

In the Attio workspace settings, open the Stripe Invoicing app page and paste the restricted Stripe API key into the connection field. The key is stored as a workspace-level connection and is only read by the app's server modules. Operators in the workspace never see the key. If the key is missing any permission the app needs, the settings panel shows a banner listing exactly which Stripe scopes to add; grant them in Stripe and reconnect.

Decide whether to sync. On the settings page, the Sync invoices toggle controls everything sync-related. Leave it on to mirror invoices into Attio (the invoices object and webhook are set up automatically when you connect). Turn it off for send-only mode, where the app still creates and sends invoices but does not build an object or process sync events. After turning sync back on, reconnect the app so the webhook is registered.

Optional advanced schema mapping. If you already have an object you want invoices to land in, turn on Show advanced schema mapping, edit the object slug and any attribute slugs to match your workspace, then click Save and set up schema. The app detects the existing object and verifies or creates attributes idempotently.

Optional workflow automation. In Attio workflows, add a Stripe trigger block (invoice finalized, paid, payment failed, or voided) to start a workflow on that event, or add a Stripe step block (create customer, create invoice, update invoice status) inside a workflow. The trigger blocks reuse the same Stripe webhook set up at connection, so no extra configuration is needed beyond a connected key.

Smoke test. Open a person record and trigger Create Invoice (it uses their email), then open a company record and trigger it (pick a person from the company). With sync on, finalize an invoice and confirm a record appears in the invoices object, then run Sync Stripe Invoices to backfill. If you built a workflow, confirm it runs when the matching invoice event fires.

To uninstall, remove the app from the workspace's installed apps page; this also removes the registered Stripe webhook. Revoking the Stripe API key from the Stripe dashboard immediately disables every call the app can make.

title: Stripe Subscriptions Integration | Attio
description: Sync Stripe subscriptions into Attio
tagline: Sync Stripe subscriptions into Attio

segments.t: Stripe Subscriptions keeps a live picture of your recurring revenue inside Attio and lets your team start new subscriptions without leaving a person record. On connection it creates a dedicated subscriptions object in your workspace and populates it from Stripe, then keeps it current automatically as subscriptions are created, updated, and canceled.

Each synced subscription carries the detail revenue and customer success teams actually need: status, product, price, recurring amount and currency, billing interval, quantity, current period start and end, start date, trial end, and whether it is set to cancel at period end. Every subscription is linked to the matching person in your workspace by email, so a contact’s recurring relationship with you sits right alongside their other CRM data. Status is stored as a status attribute, so you can group and filter subscriptions by stage, and the recurring amount is stored as a currency attribute.

The app also works in the other direction. From any person record, an operator can start a Stripe subscription in a few clicks - choosing or creating the Stripe customer, picking a product and a recurring price, setting quantity and an optional trial - and the new subscription appears in Attio immediately.

Stripe Subscriptions is workspace-scoped. It uses your own Stripe key, requires no separate Stripe account, and never stores billing data outside of Stripe and the subscriptions records it maintains in your workspace. It suits B2B SaaS, subscription, and services teams that run customer relationships in Attio and bill recurring revenue through Stripe.
Stripe Subscriptions has two directions: it syncs subscriptions from Stripe into the subscriptions object, and it creates subscriptions in Stripe from a person record.

When you connect, the app validates your Stripe key, creates a subscriptions object (and a subscriber relationship to the people object), and registers a Stripe webhook on your behalf. From then on, `customer.subscription.created`, `customer.subscription.updated`, and `customer.subscription.deleted` events flow in automatically and upsert the matching record - matched by Stripe subscription id, so re-syncing never creates duplicates. A manual sync pulls every existing subscription on demand from the settings panel or from a record action, which is useful right after install or to reconcile any missed webhook.

Each subscription is linked to a person by the Stripe customer's email. If no matching person exists, the subscription is still synced and left unlinked; you can optionally have the app create the missing person and link it. Canceled and incomplete-expired subscriptions can be synced or skipped, depending on whether you want the object to hold your full history or only live subscriptions.

To start a subscription from Attio, an operator opens a person record and triggers the create-subscription action. The app finds the person's Stripe customer by email (or creates one inline), lists your Stripe products and their recurring prices, and collects a quantity and optional trial. It then creates the subscription in Stripe and mirrors it straight into the subscriptions object.

All Stripe and Attio calls happen in server modules, never from the dialog. Incoming webhooks are verified against the Stripe signing secret before processing. Errors are surfaced as toasts and logged so they appear at the correct severity in the developer portal logs.
Stripe Subscriptions authenticates with a workspace connection holding a Stripe key. Follow these steps to install and configure the app.
Install Stripe Subscriptions into the workspace where you track recurring revenue.

Create a Stripe key in your Stripe dashboard at Developers → API keys. You can use a secret key, or a restricted key scoped to the resources the app touches. A restricted key needs write access to Customers, Products, Prices, and Subscriptions (to create subscriptions from a person record), read access to Subscriptions (to sync and validate), and read/write access to Webhook endpoints (so the app can register and remove its sync webhook).

Open the Stripe Subscriptions app in your workspace settings and paste the key into the connection field. The key is stored as a workspace connection and is only read by the app’s server code. On connect, the app validates the key, sets up the subscriptions object, and registers the webhook.

In the app’s settings panel, choose your sync options. “Auto-create missing people” creates and links a person when a subscription’s customer email has no match (off by default). “Sync canceled subscriptions” includes canceled and incomplete-expired subscriptions (on by default). Use “Sync all now” to backfill, and “Re-verify schema” to recreate the subscriptions object if it was edited or deleted.
Open any person record to find the Create Stripe Subscription action in the record action menu, and confirm the subscriptions object is populating.

To uninstall, remove the app from the workspace’s installed apps page; the app deletes its Stripe webhook during removal. Revoking the Stripe key in the Stripe dashboard immediately disables every call the app can make.

segments.t: Solvimon connects your CRM to billing infrastructure built for hybrid pricing. By syncing customer, subscription, and usage data between Attio and Solvimon, your sales team gains real-time visibility into what customers are actually using.

For companies running hybrid models (seats + usage + credits), the disconnect between CRM and billing creates blind spots. Sales reps quote customers who are already spending through PLG. Finance reconciles spreadsheets instead of closing books. Revenue leaks through the cracks between systems.
Your Attio instance becomes a single view of customer spend across self-serve and sales-led motions, and without custom orchestration code.

Built by the team that scaled Adyen's billing engine, Solvimon handles the complexity of modern monetization: multi-entity invoicing, credit burndown, usage based pricing, and enterprise contracts with commits.
The Solvimon Attio app provides:
Bi-directional customer sync.
Create a customer in Attio, and they appear in Solvimon. Update billing details in Solvimon, and they reflect in your CRM. No manual data entry, no drift between systems.
Usage and subscription visibility.

PLG + SLG unified view.
Self-serve signups and enterprise contracts appear in the same customer record. When a free user hits usage limits, sales sees the signal immediately.

between Solvimon and Attio for:
Customers and contacts
Subscriptions and their pricing tiers
Usage events and credit balances
Invoices and payment status
Custom billing attributes

app.

title: Cloudtalk Integration | Attio
description: Auto-log calls, SMS & AI insights into Attio records
tagline: Auto-log calls, SMS & AI insights into Attio records

segments.t: CloudTalk brings your team's phone conversations directly into Attio, so your CRM reflects every customer interaction without manual data entry.

Once connected, CloudTalk automatically logs calls, inbound, outbound, missed, and voicemail, and SMS to the right people along with CloudTalk's AI Conversation Intelligence: a summary, sentiment, and key topics, plus links to the recording and full call detail.

What sets CloudTalk apart is where that AI data lands. Instead of leaving AI insights trapped in a note, CloudTalk can write it into structured, filterable attributes on a call record, so you can filter, group, report, and build workflows on what was actually said, not just that a call happened.

You choose how calls are stored: as a structured Call object for teams that want to filter and report on call activity, or as simple notes for teams that want zero setup. Either way, contacts stay in sync and your reps stop copying call notes by hand.
CloudTalk supports two logging modes, so you can match the integration to how your team works.

With the custom Call object (recommended), each call becomes a structured record linked to the person, with the detail you care about written into typed attributes, direction, duration, disposition, recording link, agent, and AI summary, sentiment, and topics. Because these are real attributes, anything Attio can do with a record it can do with a call: filter, group, report, and automate. A CloudTalk call tab also appears on each person, giving reps the full call history at a glance. You map only the fields you want; anything unmapped is preserved as a note so nothing is lost.
With notes mode, each call is written as a note on the person's timeline. It's readable straight away with no configuration, ideal for smaller teams who want history without setup.
Key features:
Use any Attio list for a CloudTalk outbound dialer campaign
, CloudTalk keeps the contacts in step as people join or leave the list.
Automatic logging of inbound, outbound, missed, voicemail, transferred, and internal calls
AI call intelligence on each call, summary, sentiment, topics, and transcript link, readable on the record
Two-way contact sync, so Attio contacts power caller ID in CloudTalk and CloudTalk contacts flow into Attio, de-duplicated by email
Inbound and outbound SMS logging
Recording link on every call
One-click connection per workspace, with agents matched to users by email
Calls attributed to the real agent, matched to your workspace by email
Automatic refresh when tags, notes, or AI data arrive after a call ends
You must be a workspace admin to set up CloudTalk.

In the CloudTalk dashboard, go to Account > Integrations, find CloudTalk's Attio integration, and click Add. You'll be redirected to Attio to authorize access. Once authorized, CloudTalk imports your existing people so caller ID works from day one, and keeps them in sync automatically.
Next, choose how calls are logged:
Notes mode works immediately, with no object or field mapping. Calls and SMS appear as notes on the matching person.

Custom call object mode gives you structured, reportable calls. In Attio, create an object for your calls, add attributes for the call data you want, and add a relationship to people so calls appear on the right record. Then map your fields in the CloudTalk dashboard.

You can also choose which call types are logged, whether to include recording links, and which numbers are connected for calls and SMS. When you're ready, switch the integration to active and CloudTalk begins syncing contacts and logging conversations.
For using Attio contact lists for CloudTalk dialer campaigns:

To use an Attio list as a dialer campaign audience, CloudTalk needs read-only access to your list configuration and list entries, it reads which lists exist and who’s on them, and never changes a list or its entries.
Full setup instructions are available in CloudTalk's help center:
Configure Attio: https://help.cloudtalk.io/en/articles/16815852-configure-attio
Using CloudTalk with Attio: https://help.cloudtalk.io/en/articles/16815902-using-cloudtalk-with-attio

Furthermore, this setup supports workflow automation, allowing triggers such as sending SMS or updating CRM fields based on communication activity. Overall, the KrispCall-Attio integration saves time, reduces administrative overhead, and empowers sales, support, and customer success teams to act faster and more effectively while maintaining a consistent and professional customer experience.

title: CallPal Integration | Attio
description: Power dialing and click-to-call on your own SIP trunk
tagline: Power dialing and click-to-call on your own SIP trunk

segments.t: CallPal is an outbound calling platform for sales teams. It connects to the CRM a team already works in, brings the contacts they need to call into a calling workspace, and lets reps dial them from the browser without a desk phone or a softphone install.

Connected to Attio, CallPal reads every object in the workspace, including the ones the workspace built for itself, and makes any record carrying a phone number callable. A rep opens a record, clicks the number, and the call goes out. When there are many calls to place rather than one, the power dialer takes a selection, or one of the workspace's lists, and dials it in sequence, moving to the next record as each call ends.

Each finished call is written back to the record it came from as a note, carrying the duration, the outcome, whether a recording exists, and a link back into CallPal. The workspace stays the system of record and nobody keeps two tools in step by hand.

CallPal runs on the customer's own SIP trunk. It does not resell minutes and does not operate a shared carrier pool, so an organization keeps the carrier, the rates and the caller ID it already has, and adding a dialer never means renegotiating telephony.

Call recording is built in and treated as a compliance surface. A recording disclosure is played to the person being called before the call legs are bridged, it is on by default, and a call is dropped rather than recorded silently if the announcement cannot play. Recordings are encrypted at rest, access to them is logged, and each organization sets its own retention window.
CallPal is sold self-serve and per seat, with published pricing and a fourteen-day free trial that carries the full feature set.

CallPal syncs the following data from Attio: people, companies, deals, and any custom object your workspace has built, each with the attributes you choose to bring across. The objects are read from your workspace rather than assumed, so an object you created appears beside the standard ones. Record owners resolve to workspace member names.

Records stay in step on a schedule. A sync pulls what has changed since the last run, and a full sweep reconciles the set periodically. A record that disappears from your workspace is hidden in CallPal rather than destroyed, and only ever by a full sweep. Attributes CallPal does not recognize are kept rather than discarded, and can be promoted to columns later.

CallPal writes one thing back: a note on the record that was dialed, created when the call finishes. It carries the start time in UTC, the duration, the outcome, whether a recording exists, and a link that opens the call in CallPal. That link points into CallPal rather than at an audio file, so the recording stays behind the same permission checks it has everywhere else. Notes can be written to people, companies, deals and custom objects alike. Nothing else in your workspace is created, edited or deleted.
Delivery of that note is queued rather than fired and forgotten. If the API is briefly unavailable the write is retried, and a write that keeps failing is surfaced to an admin rather than dropped.

Reps call in two ways. Click-to-call places a single call from a record. The power dialer works a selection in sequence, with auto-advance, a progress counter, and controls to pause the campaign or pause the recording independently of it. Calls run on your own SIP trunk, so your carrier, your rates and your caller ID do not change.

A power-dialer campaign can also be filled straight from one of your Attio lists. When you create a campaign and choose "Add from Attio list", CallPal reads the names of your lists and, for the list you pick, which records are on it. Records CallPal has already synced are added to the campaign in one step; records it has not synced are counted on the form rather than dropped silently. Nothing about a list is stored, and lists are never changed.

Managers get live monitoring, listening to a call in progress, whispering to the rep without the contact hearing, or joining outright. Analytics covers answer rate, conversion, talk time, outcome mix and best time to reach, broken down by rep and by source.

Check your plan. CallPal's Attio integration is available on every CallPal plan. Starter includes one CRM integration; Pro and Scale include all of them. Every plan starts with a fourteen-day free trial that needs no card. You also need a SIP trunk from a telephony carrier: CallPal does not resell minutes, so your existing rates and caller ID carry over unchanged.

Connect the workspace. In CallPal, go to Settings, then Integrations, and choose the Attio tile. Select Continue. You will be sent to Attio to review what CallPal is asking for and approve it. Approving returns you to CallPal with the workspace connected and named on the connection.
Approve six permissions. CallPal uses each one:
Records (read): how your records are imported.
Object configuration (read): how your objects and their attributes are shown.
Notes (read-write): how a finished call is logged back onto the record.
User management (read): turns record owners into member names instead of identifiers.
List configuration (read): shows your lists by name when you fill a campaign.
List entries (read): tells CallPal which records are on the list you pick.
CallPal writes nothing to Attio except call notes; records and lists are only read.

Choose what to import. CallPal shows the objects read from your workspace, custom objects included. Select the objects you want to call, and for each one the attributes to bring across. CallPal suggests which attribute holds the name and which holds the phone number; confirm or change them. Records without a usable phone number are counted and reported rather than imported silently.
Connect a SIP trunk. Go to Settings, then SIP Trunks, and add the credentials from your carrier. Test the trunk, then activate it. Calls will not place until a trunk is active.
Set the recording policy. The disclosure played to the person being called is on by default. Set your retention window under Compliance, within the limit your plan allows.
Make the first call. Open Contacts, pick a contact, and click the number. When the call ends, open that record in Attio and the note will be on it.

Work an Attio list. On Pro and Scale, open Power Dialer, create a campaign, select "Add from Attio list", pick the list and select "Use this list". The campaign dials its records in order. A workspace connected before list support reconnects once (Settings, Integrations, Attio, Connection) to grant the two list permissions.

title: Kallio Integration | Attio
description: Connect Aircall, Dialpad, or 3CX: Calls, SMS, People
tagline: Connect Aircall, Dialpad, or 3CX: Calls, SMS, People

segments.t: Kallio connects your phone system to Attio and logs every call and text message on the person it belongs to, without anyone typing anything up.

It is built for teams on Aircall, Dialpad or 3CX who keep their customers in Attio and want the phone to show up there too. Once it is switched on, each inbound, outbound or missed call becomes a note on the matching person record, with its direction, how long it lasted and who on your team handled it. Text messages are logged the same way. People stay in step in both directions, so a person added in Attio can be recognised by your phone system, and a new caller saved in your phone system appears in Attio.

Setup takes a few minutes and needs no technical work. You sign in to your phone system and to Attio, each in a popup, choose a plan, and switch the integration on. A dashboard shows every call as it is logged, and any call from a number Attio has never seen, so nothing goes missing.
Pricing is per workspace (not per user). 7 day free trial.
Calls become notes on people

Every call your phone system completes is logged as a note on the matching person record within a few minutes of hanging up. The note carries the direction, the duration, the name of the team member who handled it, and a link back to your Kallio dashboard. Missed calls are logged too.
Text messages are logged the same way
When your phone system reports a text message, Kallio adds it as a note on the person it was sent to or received from.
Matching on the phone number

Kallio matches a call to a person by phone number, read in full international form. A number saved in Attio without a dialling code still matches, using the country you chose during setup. A call from a number no person has is kept as unmatched on the dashboard, and the moment that person is added to Attio the call is logged against them.
People stay in step

With Aircall and Dialpad, people sync both ways and keep syncing as they change. Attio tells Kallio through webhooks when a person is added, changed or removed, so Kallio hears about changes as they happen rather than by polling.
Who took the call

Every note names the team member your phone system put on the call. Kallio matches your team to your Attio workspace members by email address, and shows each person the match on their own identities page
Switched on means switched on

Connecting a system gives Kallio access and nothing more. Nothing is logged until an admin switches the integration on, and it can be paused and resumed from the dashboard at any time. Kallio keeps only the phone number, what happened and when for each call. Names and companies stay in Attio.
What you need
An Aircall, Dialpad or 3CX account you administer, an Attio account that can add apps to the workspace.
Connecting
Start from the install link.
Connect your phone system.
On the CRM step, click Connect Attio. A popup opens on Attio. Sign in if you need to, pick the workspace Kallio should work in, check what it is asking for, and approve.
Choose a plan and switch the integration on. People begin syncing straight away and calls are logged from then on.
Afterwards
Your Attio connection is listed on the Integration page under Your systems, with the workspace it is signed in as and Test and Disconnect alongside.
The full guide, including what each error on the connect step means, is at getkallio.co/docs/attio/.
