title: Swoogo Events Integration | Attio
description: The event platform that gets you so you can wow them
tagline: The event platform that gets you so you can wow them

segments.t: Sync your Swoogo events directly into Attio. This app pulls event data from your Swoogo account and creates Event records in your CRM, complete with details, timing, capacity, and attendee tracking. When registrants sign up or update their status in Swoogo, the app automatically creates or updates People records and links them to events through relationship fields, giving you a real-time view of who's registered, confirmed, checked in, or declined for each event.

What it sets up: A custom "Events" object in your Attio workspace with predefined fields for event details (name, description, status, capacity, venue type), timing (start/end dates, timezone), and attendee relationships. Optional event lists track individual registrants with their registration status and custom question responses. Widgets on both Event and People records give you quick visibility into attendance data.
Note: This app syncs events from a single Swoogo account. Registrant and contact sync are opt-in features that can be enabled in settings.

Connect Swoogo to Attio and bring your event data into your CRM automatically. The app creates an "Events" object with fields for event name, description, start/end times, timezone, status (draft, live, archived, cancelled), URL slug, domain, capacity, target attendance, registration count, and venue type.

Event sync: Use the "Sync Swoogo Events" action on any record or the batch sync in workspace settings to pull events from Swoogo into Attio. The sync is resumable, if it times out on a large event set, you can continue from where it left off. Once webhooks are active, new and updated events sync automatically in real time. Webhooks are registered with Swoogo on your behalf when you connect.

Note on large event sets: the manual sync run has a fixed time budget inside Attio's runtime. If your Swoogo account has more events than fit in a single run, the sync may stop with an "Unexpected transport error." This is expected sync is idempotent (events are deduped by Swoogo event ID), so just run "Sync Swoogo Events" again to pick up where it left off. If you have many hundreds of events to import in one shot, email us and we'll run a bulk import for you.

Registrant tracking: When registrants sign up or update their status in Swoogo, the app automatically creates People records with profile data including name, email, and job title. Registrants are linked to events through three relationship fields: Invited Attendees (waitlisted, pending, invited), Registered Attendees (confirmed, attended, checked in), and Declined Attendees (cancelled, declined). When a registrant's status changes, they're automatically moved to the correct field.

Event lists: Optionally, the app can create a dedicated list for each event containing all registrants with their registration status. If you enable custom question sync, responses to Swoogo registration questions are added as list attributes automatically.

Widgets: Event records show a registrant stats breakdown (total count plus registered, confirmed, and checked in). People records show their event attendance history with status. You must add the event widget and people widget in the configure page of the object.
Duplicate handling: Events are matched by Swoogo Event ID and registrants by email address, so duplicates are handled automatically.

Note on bulk registrant sync: The app syncs registrants in real time going forward via webhooks. For bulk importing of historical registrant data, use the batch sync in workspace settings. If you need assistance with a large historical import, contact us at
attio-apps@dialed.tech
and we can handle it for you.

Get your Swoogo API credentials: Log in to your Swoogo account, go to Settings -> API Credentials, and generate or copy your Client ID and Client Secret. The app uses OAuth2 client credentials for authentication. You must base64 encode the Client ID and Client Secret separated by a colon which can be done using a tool like
https://www.base64encode.org/
. For example: client-id:client-secret

Connect to Attio: Install the Swoogo Events app in your Attio workspace, then navigate to Workspace Settings -> Apps -> Swoogo -> Connections. Add a new connection and paste your Swoogo credentials (Client ID and Client Secret). The app will automatically create the Events object, configure relationship fields, and register webhooks with Swoogo.

Sync your events: Click "Sync Swoogo Events" to pull existing events from Swoogo into Attio. For large event sets, the sync supports batching (up to 15 batches) and resumes automatically if interrupted. Going forward, new and updated events will sync automatically via webhooks.
Configure sync options (optional):
Sync Events: Pull event data from Swoogo into Attio (enabled by default)
Sync Registrants: Sync event registrants as People records when they register or update in Swoogo (disabled by default)
Sync Contacts: Sync Swoogo contacts as People records (disabled by default)
Sync on Webhook: Automatically sync events and registrants when changes happen in Swoogo (enabled by default)
Create Event Lists: Create a dedicated Attio list for each event with registrant entries and status tracking (disabled by default)
Sync Custom Questions: Include responses to custom Swoogo registration questions as list attributes (disabled by default)

title: Clean Integration | Attio
description: Prospects backed by real-world data

segments.t: Clean is a research agent for B2B prospecting. It finds companies from what they actually do, such as loans, permits and customs shipments in public records, ranks them against your ideal customer profile, and finds the people to contact using licensed data providers. You choose which prospects to keep with Add to CRM.

The Attio app keeps your Attio workspace and Clean in step. Every prospect, company, list and custom column you keep in Clean appears in Attio, with no exports or re-typing. Edits your team makes in Attio to those people come back into Clean, and Clean recognises who is already in Attio so it never creates duplicates. People who are only in Attio stay out of Clean until you ask for them in chat and confirm.
The sync runs both ways for the people Clean sends to Attio.
What Clean writes to Attio:
People: name, email, job title, phone and their company, plus a Clean ID attribute so Clean never creates the same record twice.
Companies: name and domain.
Lists: each saved Clean list becomes an Attio people list, with its members as list entries.
Custom columns: each Clean column becomes an attribute on People (text, number, checkbox, date or select), with each person's value.
What Clean reads from Attio:

Who is already there: Clean reads the people in your Attio workspace into a private index, so it updates an existing record instead of creating a duplicate. The index never appears as prospects and is deleted when you disconnect.
Edits to synced people: a change to the name, email, job title or phone of a person Clean synced comes back into Clean.
People you ask about in chat: people who are only in Attio stay out of Clean. A member can ask Clean's chat about them, and Clean adds someone only after that member confirms it on a card.
When it syncs:
On connect, Clean backfills everything in your Clean CRM and reads the people already in Attio.
Each Add to CRM, edit, list change or new column is pushed to Attio within moments.
Clean reads Attio about every 5 minutes, and Sync now runs a full pass at any time.
Matching and safety:
People are matched by email and companies by domain, then by the Clean ID. Clean never matches by name alone.
Clean never deletes people, companies or lists in Attio. Removing a prospect from a Clean list removes only that list entry.
If a synced person is deleted in Attio, Clean stops syncing them and keeps the prospect in Clean.
Clean paces its reads and writes well under Attio's rate limits.
To stop syncing, click Disconnect in Clean (or remove the app in Attio). Clean revokes its access, and everything already written stays in your Attio workspace.

segments.t: CheckRedirects helps keep domain-based records in Attio clean and up to date.

Resolve Domain:
checks a domain or URL and returns where it ultimately resolves.
Resolve Email Domain:
extracts the root domain from an email address and checks that website.
Use them when records are created or on a recurring schedule to spot redirects, rebrands, acquisitions, dead domains, and possible duplicates.

Domain changed
is only true when the registered domain actually changes. www.acme.com → acme.com or acme.com → app.acme.com does not count; acme.com → bigcorp.com does.

Click "Add connection" and paste just the API key.
Add Resolve Domain or Resolve Email Domain to a workflow and set its input.

segments.t: Foil is first-party competitive intelligence, native to Attio.

Your reps already know why you win and lose, it's sitting in every call recording, note and closed deal in your workspace. Foil reads that history and turns it into a maintained battlecard on every competitor you come up against: win rate, the objections buyers actually raise, the feature gaps they cite, and the plays that have closed deals against them before.

Every claim is grounded in a verbatim quote and linked back to the call it came from, so a rep can trust it mid-deal, and a leader can see the evidence behind it. No analyst folklore, no enablement team maintaining a wiki that's stale by Monday. Just your own record, kept current automatically.

Battlecards live where your team already works. Reps see which competitors are in play right on the deal record, and open the full card without leaving Attio. Competitor records carry win rate, momentum and deals seen. A Battlecards list keeps every card one click away.
Foil is built for revenue teams who compete on the same handful of rivals every quarter and are tired of guessing what works against them.

Call recordings, transcripts and summaries
, the raw material Foil reads to spot when a competitor comes up and what was said about them.
Notes
, competitor mentions in written context (procurement comparisons, deal notes).
Deals and their outcomes
, closed-won and closed-lost stages, so win rate and momentum are computed from your real results.
Companies
, used once, on install, to understand what your company sells so Foil can tell "us" from "them" in a transcript.
From that, Foil:
Extracts signals.

Every competitor mention becomes a typed signal, objection, feature gap, win play, watch-out or mention, each carrying the verbatim quote and a confidence score. Low-confidence extractions queue for a quick human check…
Computes the numbers.
Win rate, deals seen and momentum per competitor, refreshed nightly from your closed deals.
Writes the battlecard back into Attio.
Competitor object, Battlecards list, per-record battlecard content, and a Competitors widget on deal records.
Setup is four one-off steps:
Set up the Competitors table view, win rate, deals seen, momentum at a glance.
Add a view to the Battlecards list Foil creates in your sidebar.
Add the Battlecard widget to Competitor records.
Add the Competitors widget to Deal records.
After that it runs on its own, as new calls and notes land, cards stay current, with every claim still cited to the call it came from.

segments.t: FolioReady is the AI-powered document collection layer for Attio. Send a branded folio request to your client, they upload their documents through a hosted portal, and FolioReady's AI reads the files and extracts the data you asked for. Every extracted value flows onto the matching Attio record automatically, a person, a company, or a deal.

This is the integration for teams that already track clients in Attio but still spend hours opening PDFs, copying out dates, account numbers, and addresses, and pasting them into custom attributes by hand. FolioReady eliminates that step. Configure your template once, choose which fields should be extracted, point each one at an Attio attribute, and the next time a client uploads documents the values land on their record without a person touching them.

Everything FolioReady writes is prefixed `folioready_` so your attribute schema stays clean and auditable. Disconnecting only stops future writes, your existing attributes and data stay put. Built for professional services teams in accounting, insurance, legal, mortgage, and consulting where every client onboarding starts with a stack of documents.

FolioReady's AI reads the content of every document a client uploads, PDFs, scanned images, photos of paperwork, and pulls out the values you configured. Each extracted value comes with a confidence rating, so high-confidence results can be accepted at a glance and lower-confidence ones flag exactly where to double-check.
Authorize FolioReady from the Attio app store. Access tokens are long-lived, so reconnection is rare.

Search your Attio people by name or email from inside FolioReady and import them as clients in two clicks. Contact details pre-fill from the matching Attio person record. Duplicate guards stop you creating the same client twice.

blocks.text: Map folio fields to Attio attributes

segments.t: In the template builder, every canvas field maps to an attribute on the Attio object the template targets, people, companies, deals, or a custom object in your workspace. Pick an existing attribute, or create a new one inline, FolioReady provisions it with a `folioready_` prefix on the object type you chose.
When a folio is completed, FolioReady writes every mapped value onto the linked Attio record. Manual fields and AI-extracted fields write through the same pipeline.

By default FolioReady syncs to Attio the moment AI processing finishes, extracted values land on the linked record and a short document synopsis posts as a note, with no one lifting a finger. The two are separate switches, so a team that wants the data on the record but would rather keep AI summaries out of the timeline turns synopses off and leaves field values running. The setting applies to the whole workspace and you can change it any time.

blocks.text: Keep uploaded files on the Attio record

segments.t: Set Attio as your file destination in FolioReady's integration settings, and every file from a completed folio attaches to the record that folio targets, the linked person, or its deal. They land in the record's own Files panel, alongside anything else your team has attached there.
Filter Attio's object settings for the `folioready_` prefix to see everything the integration manages. Disconnecting halts future writes; existing attributes remain until you delete them.
You need a FolioReady account on any plan and an Attio workspace where you have admin permissions. Admin is required so the app can create custom attributes.
Open FolioReady and go to
Settings → Integrations
Find Attio and click
Connect
. You'll be redirected to Attio.
Pick the workspace you want to connect, review the requested scopes, and authorize FolioReady.
You'll be redirected back to FolioReady with the integration marked Active.

blocks.text: AI works out of the box

Settings →
AI and pick a model for each AI action.

Template Builder
for the form you want to automate.

Create field
to provision a new `folioready_` attribute on the object type you choose.

Send the folio to a client. They upload their documents through the hosted portal. AI extraction runs as soon as files arrive, results land in the folio with confidence levels, and on completion all mapped values flow onto the linked Attio record.

Settings → Integrations
, click
Delete Connection
on the Attio integration, and confirm. Future writes stop immediately. Existing `folioready_` attributes and values remain, delete them from Attio's object settings if you want to fully remove them.

segments.t: Breakout identifies anonymous website visitors, engages them with an AI inbound SDR, and pushes qualified leads, including full conversation context, directly into Attio so your revenue team can act the moment interest strikes.

title: Echo Integration | Attio
description: Send Echo leads and replies to Attio, get deals back
tagline: Send Echo leads and replies to Attio, get deals back

segments.t: Echo is a marketing OS for small marketing teams. It shows how your brand appears in AI answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Google's AI Overviews), turns that into a to-do list of website changes, and runs your lead forms and email campaigns.

With the Echo app, Attio stays up to date with your marketing without anyone doing it by hand. Every lead Echo collects becomes a people record in Attio, every reply to an Echo email lands as a note on that person, and your Attio deals flow back into Echo. That way you can see which campaigns bring in pipeline, not just clicks.
Echo syncs right after you connect, once a day, and whenever you click "Sync now" in Echo.
From Echo to Attio

Every lead in Echo (from Echo's lead forms, email campaigns or added by your team) becomes a people record, matched by email address, so nobody is duplicated. A name already in Attio is never cleared.

Echo adds three text attributes to the people object: "Echo campaign" (the email campaign the person is in), "Echo status" (lead, sending, replied, finished, unsubscribed …) and "Echo consent" (when and how the person agreed to get email).
Replies to Echo emails are added as notes on the person. Out-of-office and other automatic replies are left out.
Only leads that changed since the last sync are written again.
From Attio to Echo

Deals created in the last 13 months (name, value, stage, won or lost) are read into Echo's Performance page. A deal whose associated person is an Echo lead counts toward that lead's campaign, so each campaign's pipeline shows next to its visits and leads.
Only when you ask
"Add to Attio" on a company that visited your website finds or creates the company record by its domain and adds a note of its visits.
Adding target accounts "From Attio" reads your company records so you can pick the ones Echo watches.
A playbook step can create or update a people record, or create an Attio task linked to the person.
Echo never deletes records, attributes or notes in Attio.

You need an Echo workspace on a paid plan (Starter, Growth or Pro). Leads, email campaigns and replies are part of Echo's Growth and Pro plans; Attio deals show on every plan. Only the owner of the Echo workspace can connect or disconnect Attio.
To connect
In Echo, go to Settings → Connections → Attio and click "Connect Attio".

Sign in to Attio, pick your workspace and allow access. Echo asks for read and write access to records (people, companies and deals), notes, tasks and object configuration (to add its three attributes to the people object), and read access to users, which Attio requires to create tasks.
You're sent back to Echo, which adds its three attributes to the people object and starts the first sync right away.
Settings → Connections → Attio then shows the Attio workspace, the last sync and how many people records and deals are linked.
To disconnect

Click "Disconnect" in the same place in Echo. Echo then forgets the connection and deletes the Attio deals it imported. Uninstalling the app in Attio (Workspace settings → Apps) also revokes Echo's access. The people records, attributes and notes Echo wrote stay in Attio.

segments.t: GetRosters Agent Check tells you which people in your Attio workspace are working real estate agents. You can filter, sort and build views on them like any other attribute, for example "GetRosters: Agent is Agent". The app writes only these six attributes and never changes anything else on your records.

"Not found" means the address is not in the GetRosters files, not that the person is not an agent. Each email address is one check, and a person with several addresses is an agent if any of them matches.
There is nothing to set up. Install the app and it is ready to use: the six GetRosters attributes are added the first time you run a check.

To see today's checks or to buy Pro, open your workspace settings, then Apps, then GetRosters Agent Check. Pro is paid on getrosters.com through Stripe and attaches to your workspace.

blocks.text: Capture contacts in person. Follow up in Attio.

segments.t: Good conversations deserve a next step. Tapify brings the people your team meets into Attio, with contact details and notes that help you follow up personally.

Exchange details through a digital business card, scan a paper business card or capture an event badge. Whether you’re meeting prospects at a conference, networking at a trade show or catching up over coffee, Tapify connects the introduction to your CRM.
Capture once. Export automatically.
Enable automatic export to send newly saved Tapify contacts to Attio as people records. Your team can focus on the conversation while exports run in the background.
Choose what you send.

Bring the details that matter.

Give every contact context.

Work with your existing CRM.
Tapify matches people by email to help avoid duplicates. Automatic exports fill empty fields while preserving existing Attio information. Manual exports update the fields you provide.
Know what’s been exported.
See export status in your Tapify dashboard, review anything needing attention and open exported contacts directly in Attio.
Connect from
Settings → Integrations → Attio
in your Tapify Teams dashboard. Authorize your Attio workspace, then choose manual export or turn on automatic export for new contacts.

title: Freelvy Integration | Attio
description: Skip existing customers and log outreach in Attio
tagline: Skip existing customers and log outreach in Attio

segments.t: Freelvy is an AI prospecting agent. Describe the customers you want to reach in plain language, and Freelvy finds the companies and people, checks their details, writes the outreach and sends it from your own mailbox.
The Attio app connects Freelvy to your workspace so that prospecting respects what you already know.
Freelvy never contacts people or companies that are already in Attio, are customers, or have an open deal.
New prospects are added as people and company records, without duplicates and without overwriting anything you already have.
Every email sent and reply received is kept as a note on the record.
When a prospect is interested or books a meeting, Freelvy opens a deal and adds a task to reply within 24 hours.

You stay in control. You choose what is skipped, when prospects are added, what is logged and which deal stage is used. Only the owner of the Freelvy account can change these settings, and you can disconnect at any time.
People (by email address) and companies (by domain) are read before each campaign, so Freelvy never contacts someone you already know.
Deals are read to find open deals and won deals. A deal in a stage whose name contains "Won" counts as a customer, and its people and company are skipped.
Changes in Attio are picked up through a signed webhook, and the list is also refreshed regularly. Deal outcomes are read back, so the exclusion list stays current.
Prospects: people and company records are matched on email address or domain, so no duplicates are created. An existing record is only completed where a field is empty.
Attributes: Freelvy adds its own attributes, all starting with "Freelvy" (origin, campaign, signal, location, company size, industry, lead source, reply category).
History: a note on the record for each email sent and reply received, copied to the deal when there is one.
Deals: when a prospect is interested or books a meeting, a deal is created at the stage you chose, with the reply as a note and a task to reply within 24 hours.
The deals object is optional in Attio and may be turned off in your workspace. If it is off, Freelvy still skips people and logs the history, and tells you to ask a workspace admin to enable it.
In Freelvy, open Settings, then Integrations, and choose Attio.
Select Connect Attio, sign in to Attio and approve the requested permissions. Freelvy never sees your password.
Freelvy creates its attributes and a webhook, and adds the Interested and Meeting booked deal stages if you allow it.
Only one CRM can be connected to a Freelvy account at a time.
Skip people already in Attio: choose among people already in Attio, customers, and people with an open deal.
Add prospects to Attio: when a campaign starts, when you approve a row, or never.
Keep the history: emails sent and replies.
Deals: create a deal when someone is interested or books a meeting, pick the stage for each case, and add a task to reply within 24 hours.

Freelvy asks to read and write records, to configure objects (to add its attributes), to write notes and tasks, to manage a webhook and to read workspace members. Deals are owned by the member who authorized the app.
Select Disconnect in the same card. Freelvy stops writing to Attio and removes its webhook. What is already in Attio stays there.

segments.t: involve.me is the AI quiz funnel builder with built-in email automation, best for businesses where every qualified lead is worth hundreds or thousands of dollars.

Use it to create quizzes, assessments, calculators, product recommendation flows, landing pages, and forms that capture leads, qualify them with scores and logic, segment them by fit or intent, and automatically send personalized email sequences based on answers, outcomes, scores, variables, opens, and clicks. Unlike quiz builders that only capture a lead and hand it off, involve.me connects the quiz funnel directly to the follow-up journey.
AI Agent.
Generates and edits complete funnels through chat: flow structure, routing logic, copy, design, scoring rules, formulas, and outcome pages with personalized charts, gauges, and graphs.
Built-in email automation.

Every submission creates a contact in involve.me with mapped properties and segments, then enters email sequence workflows that branch on answers, scores, outcomes, opens, and clicks. OTP verification on email and SMS blocks junk submissions before they enter any workflow.
Integrations.

With Attio connected, every qualified lead and its funnel data lands in your CRM the moment a funnel is submitted, alongside 50+ other native data integrations, 3 payment integrations, 5 tracking integrations, Zapier, and webhooks.

Best for high-ticket service businesses (financial advisors, insurance brokers, legal, real estate, mortgage, solar, med spas, education providers), expert-led businesses (coaches, consultants, advisors, course creators, assessment-based experts), and high-consideration product businesses (skincare, wellness, furniture, mattresses, B2B software, custom products).
SOC 2 Type 2 audited, GDPR-compliant. Trusted by 4,500+ businesses globally.
When a respondent submits a funnel, involve.me sends the following data to Attio:
Respondent details: name, email, phone, company, and any other collected fields
Funnel data: answers, outcome, score, calculator results, variables
list assignment in Attio
Each funnel maps its own fields to Attio people / companies attributes, so different quizzes write into the record on their own schema. Data syncs on every completed submission.
In the involve.me funnel editor, open the Connect tab and select Attio.
Authorize the connection with your Attio workspace.
Map funnel fields to Attio attributes (and choose the target object / list).
Publish the funnel. Submissions sync to Attio automatically.
The Attio integration is available on the Grow plan and above.

description: Automatically sync Calendly bookings to Attio

segments.t: This Attio app automatically syncs your Calendly booking data into your CRM. It creates People records from meeting attendees, tracks booking events, and captures form answers in structured lists.
This app will work on all Attio plan tiers and does not require any custom objects.
This app currently supports
Calendly scheduling
and
routing form
submissions. The app requires a paid Calendly subscription
We welcome feedback and would love to hear any ideas you have for what to build next.
Drop us a note
. If you're looking for other useful apps we've published, check out
Duplicate Detection
Advanced Workflow Automations
, or explore everything we offer on the
Neon Deer platform
to learn more.

Connect your Calendly account to Attio to automatically sync booking data in real-time. The app creates two lists in Attio: "Calendly Booking Events" for each booking with full event details, and "Calendly Answers" for all question/answer pairs from booking forms.

The integration automatically creates people records for invitees and guests, tracks reschedules and cancellations, captures payment information (payment provider, amount, currency, and status), and links all related data together. You can filter which users and event types to sync through workspace settings, but by default the app will capture everything.
Get your Calendly token from an Admin
Log in to your Calendly account
Go to "Integrations & apps" >> "API and webhooks"
Generate a Personal Access Token. Ensure that the Personal Access Token (PAT) has the following scopes: users:read
event_types:read
routing_forms:read
scheduled_events:read
webhooks:read
webhooks:write
Connect to Attio
Install the Calendly Events app in your Attio workspace
Navigate to Workspace Settings → Connections
Add a new connection and paste your Calendly Personal Access Token
The app will automatically create webhook subscriptions, provision lists, and configure handlers
Configure filtering (optional)
User Email Whitelist
- Comma-separated list of Calendly user emails. Leave empty to sync all users.
Event Whitelist
- Comma-separated list of event identifiers. Leave empty to sync all event types. Use asterisks to configure wildcard matching, for example *demo to match all events ending with "demo" in the URL
Auto-create people
- Toggle to automatically create people records for invitees and guests.
The setup typically completes within a few minutes. Once active, the integration will automatically sync new bookings, reschedules, and cancellations to your Attio workspace.

segments.t: Generate beautiful forms from your Attio workspace schema.

This app reads your Attio objects and attributes to build forms that write submissions directly into your CRM. No Zapier, no spreadsheets, no manual entry. Choose any object, pick your fields, and get a shareable public URL in minutes.
What it sets up:
A hosted form builder connected to your Attio workspace. Forms are schema-aware, so field types (text, select, email, number) match your Attio attributes automatically.
Note:
Attio Forms supports multi-workspace connections, so you can manage forms across multiple Attio workspaces from a single account.
Build forms from your CRM schema.
Connect your Attio workspace and the app pulls in your objects and attributes. Select an object, drag and drop the fields you want, and your form is ready to share.
Direct CRM writes:
Every submission creates or updates a record in Attio instantly. Related objects are linked automatically. No middleware, no sync delays.
Customize the look:
Apply custom CSS, add your logo, and style forms to match your brand. Forms are mobile-responsive out of the box.
Share anywhere:
Each form gets a public URL you can send to prospects, embed in emails, or link from your website. OpenGraph metadata means clean previews when shared on social.
Sign up at
attioforms.com
Create an account and connect your Attio workspace. The app uses OAuth so your API credentials stay secure.
Select an object
Choose the Attio object you want to collect data for (e.g., Companies, People, or any custom object).
Build your form
Use the drag-and-drop builder to add fields. The app reads your workspace schema, so field types and select options match Attio automatically.
Configure related objects (optional)
Link submissions to related records in Attio. For example, associate a new Person with an existing Company.
Customize and publish
Add your logo, apply custom CSS if you want, and hit publish. You get a public URL to share immediately.
Setup takes under five minutes. Submissions start flowing into Attio as soon as your form is live.

title: Ikiform Integration | Attio
description: Send website form submissions to Attio as people
tagline: Send website form submissions to Attio as people

segments.t: Ikiform is a form backend for websites. Point any HTML form, framework or site builder at your Ikiform endpoint and every submission is stored, checked for spam and sent where your team works.

The Ikiform app turns each new form submission into a person in Attio. Ikiform finds the person by email, creates them if they're new, fills the attributes you mapped and saves the whole submission to them as a note, with a link back to it in Ikiform. Use it for contact, demo request, sales and signup forms, so every lead lands in Attio without copying data by hand or adding an automation tool in between.
When a form gets a new submission, Ikiform:
Looks up the person in Attio by email address.
Creates the person if they don't exist yet, or updates the attributes you mapped if they do.
Adds the person to a list you choose, if you picked one, and sets any fixed value you chose, such as a lead source.
Adds a note to the person with every field of the submission and a link to it in Ikiform.

Common fields like name, phone and job title are mapped for you, and you can change any of them in the field mapping editor. Spam is never sent to Attio. Failed sends are retried automatically, and retries never create a duplicate person, list entry or note.

Ikiform reads your person attributes, lists and workspace members so you can map fields, and writes people, list entries and notes. It only writes to the People object, the list you pick and notes on people.
You need an Ikiform account. Integrations are included on every Ikiform plan at no extra cost.
Sign in at ikiform.com and create a form, or open one you already have.
Open Integrations, choose Attio, then Connect Attio and approve access for your workspace.
In your form's Integrations tab, choose Add integration, then Attio.
Open Field mapping to check which form fields go to which person attributes. Optionally pick a list to add each person to.
Choose Send test to create a test person, then submit your form.
To disconnect, remove the connection in Ikiform under Integrations, Attio. Ikiform revokes its access in Attio when you do.

description: Turn landing page leads into Attio people records
tagline: Turn landing page leads into Attio people records

segments.t: PageKiss is an AI-powered website and landing page builder that helps businesses create and publish websites, capture leads and grow their online presence without coding.
With the Attio integration, every new inquiry from your PageKiss forms is added to Attio as a person record automatically. No manual data entry, no lost leads, and your team can follow up right away.
PageKiss sends new leads from your website and landing page forms to Attio.
Lead data flows one way, from PageKiss to Attio. When a visitor submits a connected form, PageKiss creates a new record in your People object.
Depending on your form and field mapping, this can include:
Email address
First and last name
Phone number
Company name
Additional details, such as an inquiry message or service of interest
Values for existing custom attributes on People

PageKiss uses AI to match your form fields to attributes that already exist in People. Fields without a suitable match are not sent to Attio and stay in the saved PageKiss lead. PageKiss reads your People attributes only to suggest the mapping. It does not change your workspace settings or create new attributes.
PageKiss saves every submission before sending it to Attio and shows the delivery status in Forms → Leads. If delivery fails, the submission stays in PageKiss so your team can follow up.
Updating or merging existing records, syncing changes back to PageKiss, and creating deals, lists or other objects.

Open your project in the PageKiss editor and ask the assistant in the chat to connect your form to Attio (for example, "Connect my contact form to Attio"). You can also go to Forms → Where leads go → Add integration.
Click Connect on the Attio card.
Sign in to Attio, choose the workspace where leads should arrive, review the permissions and click Allow.
When you see "Success", click Finish. Attio now shows as Connected on your form.
PageKiss maps your form fields to your People attributes automatically. If you change the form, publish the page to refresh the mapping.
Publish your page, submit a test entry, then check its delivery status in Forms → Leads and find the new person in Attio People.

In Forms → Where leads go, click the power icon to pause delivery for a form, or the unplug icon to detach Attio from it. To disconnect the workspace connection, go to Settings → Connections and choose Disconnect.
An Attio administrator can open Workspace settings → Apps, select PageKiss and choose Uninstall. Records already created stay in Attio, and saved submissions stay in PageKiss.

Business owners simply describe what they offer, who they serve, and their pricing, and the platform automatically creates polished pages with copy, imagery, calls-to-action, and a search-ready structure. Every site is editable in real time from both mobile and desktop, making it easy to update content between jobs or at the office.

built-in growth tools
that eliminate the need for third-party plugins:
Instant quote calculators
that convert visitors into leads
Form submissions and contact blocks
that notify owners immediately
Online booking and appointment scheduling
eCommerce and payments
for products, deposits, and service packages
Events, galleries, and portfolios
for showcasing work

SiteSeam is built for real-world operators, home service businesses, local shops, consultants, and solo professionals, who want one platform to
build their website, generate leads, accept payments, and manage growth
from a single dashboard. Pricing starts under $10/month, with unlimited usage of all core features as businesses scale.
In short, SiteSeam replaces fragmented tools with a single AI-driven system that helps small businesses look established, convert visitors, and grow, starting on day one.

We connect your SiteSeam account to Attio so every meaningful lead interaction flows into your CRM automatically. When someone reaches out, subscribes, books time, or requests an instant quote, their details are captured in Attio and logged with clear notes so your team can follow up fast without manual data entry. This keeps your pipeline current, your team aligned, and your response times faster, while keeping each client’s data securely separated.

To configure the Attio CRM in SiteSeam, go to Settings → Integrations, find the Attio card, and click “Connect Attio.” You’ll be redirected to Attio to authorize SiteSeam; choose the workspace you want to sync and approve access. When you return to SiteSeam, the Attio connection will appear in the Attio connections list, use “List Connections” to confirm the workspace, reconnect if needed, or disconnect it at any time.

title: Jira Sync Integration | Attio
description: Automatically sync data between Jira and Attio
tagline: Automatically sync data between Jira and Attio

segments.t: Jira Sync automatically syncs and displays connected Jira Cloud account data in your Attio records. Revenue, support, and operations teams can create or link Jira issues from the records they already use, then follow progress without leaving Attio.

The linked Jira issues widget shows the current summary, status, priority, assignee, Jira link, and unread comment activity. When relevant, it also shows other affected Attio records or linked deal value. Users can update supported issue fields, open the shared comment thread, or unlink an issue from a record.

Jira Sync also adds selected-record actions and workflow blocks. Create an issue for one record, create issues for many selected records, link an existing issue to one or many records, or automate issue creation and linking in Attio workflows. Created and linked issues are available to later workflow blocks, allowing the issue key, URL, status, and other details to drive downstream steps.
Jira webhooks keep linked issue details and comment notifications current. An optional resolved-issue follow-up can create an Attio task when a linked issue moves to Jira's Done status category.
Jira Sync is designed for customer-facing teams that need a clear connection between customer records in Attio and product, engineering, or service work in Jira.

Open an Attio record and use the Jira Sync actions to create a Jira issue or link an existing one. When creating an issue, select the Jira project, issue type, and optional priority, then write the summary and description.

Summary and description templates can combine your own text with variables from the current Attio record. Jira Sync resolves those variables separately for each record and adds a link back to Attio, keeping the issue connected to its customer context. If the description is left empty, the app uses its default Attio context when a record is linked.
Selected-record actions support bulk work. You can create one Jira issue for each selected Attio record or link one existing issue to multiple selected records.

The linked Jira issues widget refreshes issue details from Jira and displays the current status, priority, assignee, recent comment activity, and a direct Jira link. Depending on the linked data, it can also show other affected Attio records and linked deal value.

From Attio, users can edit a linked issue's summary, priority, assignee, or status. They can also view the Jira comment thread and add attributed comments. A user may edit or delete comments that they added through Attio. New Jira comments appear as a per-user unread badge until that user opens the comment thread.
Jira Sync registers dynamic webhooks for issue changes, issue deletion, and comment activity. These events refresh linked data and comment notifications in Attio.

If an issue is deleted in Jira, the workspace can automatically remove its links and stored notification data. Alternatively, the app can keep the link visible as unavailable until a user unlinks it manually.

When resolved-issue follow-up is enabled, Jira Sync creates a native Attio task on every linked record when an issue enters Jira's Done status category. Repeated webhook deliveries are deduplicated, and reopened issues can create a new task when resolved again.

The Create Jira issue workflow block creates an issue from workflow text and variables and can optionally link it to a target Attio record through the Record to link field. By selecting variable for example, Record Created > Created user, the created user object will display a widget about the created Jira issue.
The Link Jira issue block connects an existing Jira issue to a target record.
Both blocks return structured issue details to later workflow blocks, including the Jira issue ID, key, URL, summary, status, priority, project, issue type, and cloud ID.
Install Jira Sync in your Attio workspace.
Open Workspace Settings > Apps > Jira Sync.
Open the Connections tab and connect the workspace to Jira Cloud through OAuth.
Approve access with a Jira account that can view the required projects and perform the Jira actions your team will use.
Open the Jira Sync Settings tab and configure the Jira Cloud connection.
Select the Jira site.
Select the default project.
Select the default issue type.
Optionally select a default priority, or leave it set to Use Jira default.
Select Check connection.
Checking the connection validates Jira access and creates or renews the dynamic webhooks used for issue and comment updates. You do not need to create a Jira webhook manually.
Choose whether deleted Jira issues should be automatically unlinked from every associated Attio record. Automatic unlinking also clears stored link and comment-notification data.

Optionally enable resolved-issue follow-up. Set the number of days until the task is due and optionally select a default Attio assignee. Jira Sync will create a native Attio task on each linked record when the Jira issue moves to the Done status category.

Open a record and select Create Jira issue or Link Jira issue from its available actions. Complete the required Jira fields and, when creating an issue, use the variable browser to add values from the current record to the summary or description.
To work with several records, select them in an Attio table and run Create Jira issues or Link Jira issue from the selected-record actions.
Create or edit an Attio workflow and add the appropriate Jira Sync block.

Create Jira issue creates a new issue. To link it, use Record to link and select a record from the trigger or an earlier block. Jira Sync detects the record's object type automatically. Leave Record to link empty for a standalone issue.
Link Jira issue connects an existing issue to a target record.

Use Attio's workflow variable picker in the summary, description, issue key, or target record fields as applicable. Connect the Jira issue created or Jira issue linked outcome to later blocks when the workflow needs to use the returned issue details, then publish the workflow.

Jira Sync includes a 14-day free trial. A workspace admin can start the trial and manage the paid plan from the app's settings page. Paid plans are based on the number of users in the Attio workspace.

description: AI that knows your product, your team, and everything about

segments.t: Revo is an AI superintelligence workspace that compounds organizational knowledge for product teams, turning fragmented data into persistent insights and aligned actions. Our Attio integration syncs your CRM deals, relationships, and customer data seamlessly into Revo's Intelligence Modules, eliminating silos and enabling AI-driven analysis across tools like Jira or Slack.

Imagine pulling Attio pipeline trends to auto-generate PRDs, flag churn risks from interaction data, or create workflows that update deals based on product feedback. This bidirectional sync lets you push Revo insights (e.g., sentiment analyses or prioritization scores) back to Attio, creating a living loop that gets smarter over time. Ideal for revenue-focused productマネ teams in startups and enterprises, it saves hours on manual aggregation, reduces misalignment, and accelerates shipping by tying customer intel directly to roadmaps. With OAuth setup and SOC 2 compliance, it's secure and scalable, no more jumping between apps. Unlock superintelligence for your CRM data today.
Revo's Attio integration works by securely syncing CRM data via OAuth, processing it through our AI modules, and enabling automations for product teams. Here's the flow:
Connection Setup
: From Revo's Integrations settings, connect Attio, grant scopes for reading/writing deals, contacts, and notes. Revo pulls initial data (e.g., pipelines, interactions) into dedicated modules.
Data Syncing

: Real-time or scheduled pulls bring Attio objects into Revo. For example, sync deal stages for trend analysis or customer notes for sentiment insights. Bidirectional: Push Revo-generated data (e.g., AI-prioritized tasks) back as Attio updates or comments.
AI Processing
: Revo's modules compound Attio data with other sources, e.g., cross-reference deal feedback with Jira issues to auto-flag product gaps or generate reports like "Top customer pains from Q3 deals."
Workflows & Insights

: Build no-code automations, such as alerting on stalled deals or creating PRDs from interaction trends. Proactive suggestions appear in chat (e.g., "This Attio deal mentions feature X, add to roadmap?").
Security & Revocation
: Data is encrypted, access-logged, and ephemeral, revoke anytime via Revo or Attio dashboards.
This creates a unified CRM-product brain, evolving smarter with every sync.
Setting up the Revo-Attio integration is quick and secure, takes under 5 minutes. Follow these steps:
Access Integrations in Revo
: Log into your Revo workspace, go to Settings > Integrations, and search for Attio.
Connect Account
: Click 'Connect', you'll be redirected to Attio for OAuth authorization. Log in and grant permissions (e.g., read/write on deals, contacts). Revo uses minimal scopes for security.
Configure Sync Settings
: Choose data to sync (e.g., specific pipelines, custom fields) and set frequency (real-time via webhooks or scheduled). Map Attio objects to Revo modules (e.g., deals to Insights).
Test the Connection
: Run a manual sync to verify, Revo will pull sample data and generate a test insight. Check for errors in the integration status log.
Customize Workflows
: In Revo, create automations (e.g., "On new Attio deal, analyze notes and flag product trends"). Add human approvals if needed.
Troubleshoot/Revoke
: If issues arise, check Revo's logs or Attio's audit trail. Revoke via Revo settings or Attio apps page, data sync stops immediately.
For advanced setups (e.g., custom mappings), contact Revo support. No coding required, start compounding Attio data today!

title: UseReviews Integration | Attio
description: Turn customer feedback into insights tied to every person
tagline: Turn customer feedback into insights tied to every person

segments.t: UseReviews is a voice-of-customer platform for SaaS teams. It pulls in customer feedback from reviews, surveys, support conversations and in-app widgets, uses AI to turn it into insights (churn signals, bug reports, feature requests, competitor mentions and advocates) and ties every piece of feedback to the person who gave it.

The Attio app puts that evidence where your team already works. Each company and person in Attio shows what customers are saying and how they use your product, so account owners can see churn risk, open requests and advocates without leaving their CRM.

UseReviews collects what your customers say (reviews, support tickets, calls, surveys) and turns it into churn signals, bug reports and feature requests. Connect Attio and those signals appear on the companies and people your team already works with.
Companies
, matched to your UseReviews accounts by domain: the MRR, plan and renewal date attributes you choose, and the record owner.
People
, matched by email address, and a lifecycle stage attribute if you choose one.
Deals
on linked companies: value, stage, owner and associated company.
Workspace members

(read only, user_management:read): Attio stores a company’s or deal’s owner as a workspace member ID. UseReviews reads your workspace members to turn that ID into the owner’s name, shown on the account and its deals in UseReviews. It never changes members.
UseReviews never creates companies or people in Attio and never changes your own attributes.
What UseReviews writes to Attio
UseReviews creates its own attributes and writes only to those.
Companies:
UseReviews: Insights
(usereviews_insights): one line each for open churn signals, bugs and feature requests with their status, competitors and advocates.
UseReviews: Account usage
(usereviews_usage, with Pulse): the account’s product usage state.
UseReviews: Link
(usereviews_link): a link to the account in UseReviews.
People:
UseReviews: Insights
(usereviews_person_insights): the same kind of lines as the company’s, but only what this person raised.
UseReviews: Advocate
(usereviews_advocate): whether the person is an advocate.
UseReviews: Usage
(usereviews_product_usage, with Pulse): New, Active, Slipping or Dormant.
UseReviews: Activated
(usereviews_activated, with Pulse): whether the person activated.
These attributes hold only summaries, never customer quotes.
Timeline notes
UseReviews adds a note to the company’s timeline for these five events, and no others. Each can be switched off in UseReviews settings.
New churn signal
: includes a quote of what the customer said (up to 300 characters) and the name of who said it.
New bug report
: includes a quote of what the customer said (up to 300 characters) and the name of who said it.
New feature request
: includes a quote of what the customer said (up to 300 characters) and the name of who said it.
Feature request shipped
: a feature request the company made has shipped. No quote.
Bug fixed
: a bug the company reported was fixed. No quote.
Each note links to the card in UseReviews. Notes cover only what happens after you connect, never old history.
Keeping in sync

Attio notifies UseReviews when a company, person or deal changes, and changes are read and written every 15 minutes. Everything is read again once a night. Disconnecting removes the webhook; attributes and notes already written stay in Attio.
You need a UseReviews workspace and the Owner or Admin role to connect Attio.
In UseReviews, go to Settings → Integrations and click Connect Attio.
Approve access to your Attio workspace.
Optionally, choose which Attio attributes hold MRR (and whether it’s monthly or annual), plan, renewal date and lifecycle stage.
Switch off any write-back attribute or timeline note type you don’t want. Changes apply from the next sync.

To disconnect, go to Settings → Integrations in UseReviews. This deletes the stored tokens and removes the webhook UseReviews registered in Attio. The usereviews_ attributes stay on your records with their last values, and notes already added stay on the timeline; you can delete them in Attio. The app stays installed in Attio, so uninstall it there if you don’t plan to reconnect.

title: ProBackup Integration | Attio
description: Automated daily backups & one-click restore for Attio
tagline: Automated daily backups & one-click restore for Attio

blocks.text: Automated daily backups and one-click restore for Attio.

segments.t: ProBackup is an independent backup service for Attio CRM. It creates a daily Snapshot of your workspace and stores it outside Attio, so you can restore a single record (or a whole list) exactly as it existed on any earlier date.

Every Snapshot captures records (people, companies, deals, users and workspaces), lists, files, comments, notes and tasks. Backups run once every 24 hours. Connect Attio via secure OAuth in around three minutes; there is nothing to install and nothing for your team to maintain.

blocks.text: Why your CRM needs a backup of its own

segments.t: Attio protects its own infrastructure. It does not protect you from your own workspace: a deleted record, a bulk edit that overwrites the wrong field across hundreds of companies, a departing colleague's cleanup, or an automation or AI agent acting faster than anyone can notice. Recovering that data is your responsibility, and that is the gap ProBackup fills.

Restore exactly what you lost: an individual record, a comment, a note, a file, a task, or a full list, without rolling back the work your team has done since. Point-in-time recovery lets you choose the date to restore from.

Vault gives you a structured view of your backed-up Attio data. Navigate your workspace hierarchy, switch between data types, use the date picker to see how records evolved, and compare versions side by side. Export any table to Excel. Global search across every Snapshot is available on Pro and Premium plans.

blocks.text: Redundant Google Drive sync (Pro and Premium)

segments.t: Sync backups to Google Sheets and Drive folders for a second copy in a format your team already knows: readable even if ProBackup is unavailable.
Get an email when ProBackup detects unusual deletion volume or a sharp drop in backed-up records, so you find out before the damage compounds.

AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS in transit, two-factor authentication and Google SSO on all plans. Premium adds Single Sign-On, audit reports, a virus scanner, bulk file download and advanced scope control.

Plans start at $25/month billed annually ($31 monthly). Pro is $38 ($47) and Premium is $69 ($86). Your subscription covers unlimited apps: back up Attio alongside 20+ other platforms under one licence. Version history runs 6 months on Plus and 2 years on Pro. Start a free 7-day trial; no credit card required.

You authorise ProBackup from your Attio account using secure OAuth, no API keys to generate, no credentials stored, nothing to install. Setup takes around three minutes. You then select which workspaces to include or exclude from scope. Access can be revoked from Attio at any time.

ProBackup reads your Attio data through the official Attio API once every 24 hours. There is no schedule to configure. Each run produces a Snapshot: a complete, dated version of your workspace rather than a delta, so any single date can be restored on its own.
The backup is read-only. ProBackup writes nothing back to Attio unless you explicitly trigger a restore, so your workspace, automations and audit trail are unaffected by the backup itself.

API rate limits and transient errors are handled by the backup engine, which reschedules failed calls automatically instead of skipping the affected data. You do not need to intervene when a run hits a limit.
Each Attio Snapshot includes:
Records
, people, companies, deals, users and workspaces, with their attribute values
Lists
, including list entries and their structure
Notes
and
comments
Tasks
Files
and attachments, stored as files rather than links

ProBackup captures what the Attio API exposes. Anything the API does not make available cannot be backed up by any third-party tool, ours included, we would rather state that than imply coverage we cannot deliver.

Snapshots are stored on AWS S3, encrypted with AES-256 at rest and transferred over TLS. Your backups sit outside Attio's infrastructure, so a problem inside your Attio workspace, a deletion, a bad bulk edit, a misfiring integration, has no effect on the stored copies. Account access is protected by two-factor authentication and Google SSO on all plans; Premium adds Single Sign-On.

Every daily Snapshot is retained as a separate version, so you can compare how a record changed over time and restore the state from a specific date. Version history covers 6 months on Plus and 2 years on Pro.
Restores are granular and run through the Attio API. Select a record, note, comment, task, file or list, choose the date, and restore it, without rolling back changes your team made afterwards.

blocks.text: 8. Optional Google Drive sync (Pro and Premium)

segments.t: Records are written to Google Sheets and updated daily; files are stored separately in Drive folders. Sheet cell limits (2 million per sheet) are handled automatically. Above 50,000 records no Sheet is created, though the AWS backup continues to run in full.

You need an Attio account and a ProBackup account. Registration is by email (passwordless by default), with optional password and two-factor authentication, or SSO on Premium. No credit card is required for the 7-day trial, and nothing is installed in your Attio workspace.
Sign up at probackup.io and confirm your email address.
Choose Attio from the list of supported platforms. You can add other platforms to the same account at any time (your subscription covers unlimited apps).
You are redirected to Attio to approve the connection. ProBackup requests read access to your workspace data; approval takes one click, and you can revoke it from Attio whenever you choose.
Select which data types to include or exclude.

blocks.text: 5. Enable Google Drive sync (optional, Pro and Premium)

segments.t: Connect Google Drive to keep a second copy of your backups in Google Sheets and Drive folders, updated daily.
Your first backup begins immediately. After that, ProBackup runs once every 24 hours with no further input. You can follow progress from the dashboard.

Invite colleagues and set permissions per platform: View only, Export, or Restore. You also choose whether an invited user sees all backed-up data or only the data they can already access in Attio. Plus includes 1 user, Pro includes 10, and Premium is unlimited.

title: PublicViews Integration | Attio
description: Share the view - Keep the workspace
tagline: Share the view - Keep the workspace

segments.t: Share the view. Keep the workspace.

PublicViews is how you get information out of Attio and in front of someone who is not in your workspace: a client, an investor, a candidate, a partner, a contractor. You choose a list or an object, narrow it to the records that person should see, switch on the attributes they should see, and publish the result as a web page at its own address. You send one link. They open it. There is no account for them to create, no invitation to accept, and no Attio seat to pay for.

Attio has no way to show a list to someone outside your workspace. The alternatives are a CSV that is wrong by Thursday, a paid seat so one person can read eight records, or rebuilding the whole thing somewhere else and maintaining it twice. This is the fourth option.

The product is built around what a viewer cannot reach. A new page starts with every attribute hidden, so nothing is exposed until you expose it, and an attribute you did not switch on is not sent to the browser at all. The link carries its own locks, and they stack rather than replace one another: an unlisted address, a password, an email or domain allowlist, and an expiry by date or by number of opens. Row scoping goes further and shows each viewer only the records matched to the address they confirmed, so one link can serve every client their own rows.

A viewer can change nothing you have not marked editable, and a new page marks nothing. Where you have allowed it, a viewer proposes a value and you decide how it lands. It can wait in your dashboard beside the value Attio holds now until you approve it, which is the default and how every page starts, or it can apply on its own. Both require the viewer to confirm their email address first, and either way the change is recorded with the value it replaced, so you can see what happened and put it back.
PublicViews is built by Dialed Technologies. It is an independent app and is not an official Attio product.
PublicViews syncs the following data from Attio, and nothing else.
Attribute schemas, for the objects and lists you choose to publish from: attribute names, types and select options. This is what lets you choose columns and build filters.

Record values, for the records your filter matches, and only for the attributes you have made visible. An attribute you leave hidden is not stored and is not sent to a browser. Stored beside each row are the Attio record identifier, the list entry identifier where the source is a list, and the parent object slug.

Workspace members, as a directory: member identifier, display name, email address and avatar URL. It is refreshed at most once a day and exists so that an attribute holding a workspace member renders a name rather than an identifier. A member's email address reaches a viewer only if you made that attribute visible.
PublicViews reads through your own Attio account, so it can never reach a record you could not open yourself.

It writes one thing back: a change a viewer made to an attribute you marked editable, either after you approve it or, if you chose that mode, on its own. Each one is recorded with the value it replaced. Nothing else is ever written to Attio.

A published page is served from this stored copy rather than from a call to Attio, so viewer traffic never touches your Attio rate limit. PublicViews re-reads Attio on a schedule set by your plan and the size of the source. Every published page carries the time it last updated, and you can start a sync yourself before a call. Pausing a page is one click and its address stops resolving. Deleting your PublicViews workspace deletes the stored copy with it.

You do not need a paid plan to use this app. The PublicViews free plan covers one published page, does not expire and does not ask for a card. Paid plans raise the number of pages, the size of a source and how often it re-reads Attio.
You do need an Attio account that can already see the records you want to publish. PublicViews reads through your own account and can never reach more than you can.
Create a PublicViews account
Sign up at publicviews.app/sign-up.
Connect your Attio workspace
Open Settings, then Attio, and start the connection. Approve Attio's consent screen and you are returned with the workspace connected.

Expect that screen to ask for write access, and do not read anything into it. Attio fixes an app's scopes at registration and offers no way to narrow them per install, so every publisher consents to the same set whether or not any page they build is ever editable. What decides whether PublicViews writes is PublicViews: viewer edits are off on a new page, and turning them on takes several deliberate steps the app shows you as a checklist.
Create a page

Choose New view and pick the list or object it reads from. Setting up a draft is three steps: Data, Access, Publish. Each step saves before the next one opens, and nothing is public until the last one.

Data. Choose which records the page covers: everything in the list or object, one of your Attio saved views, or conditions you build yourself. Then choose the columns. Every attribute starts hidden, and you cannot leave this step with all of them hidden.

Access. Choose between an unlisted link, a password, an email or domain allowlist, and an expiry, and combine as many as the situation deserves. Row scoping is optional and shows each viewer only the records matched to the address they confirmed. Viewer edits are set here: a new page allows none, and you can let changes wait for your approval or apply on their own.

Publish. The last step shows the page as your viewer will get it, beside a manifest of what is shared, what is sensitive and what is withheld. Publishing is gated: the app lists every reason it will not publish, with a code and the control that clears it. There is no publish anyway.
After it is published

The same address opens an editor with five rows, each expanding in place: Rows, Columns, Access, Look and Activity. Proposed edits and visit counts are under Activity. Approving an edit writes it to Attio; rejecting it changes nothing there.
